articles.title: 'It's incredible,' Winnipeg man says after car blows over onto someone else's lawn in storm
articles.summary: A Winnipeg man says the damage left by Sunday night's thunderstorm was "overwhelming," after his vehicle rolled into the front yard of a nearby home.

image.caption: Darryl Gervais says winds during Sunday night's thunderstorm pushed his car so hard that it rolled over into a nearby lawn on Lindsay Street in Winnipeg's River Heights area. (Gavin Axelrod/CBC)

blocks.text: Manitoba·Updated
A Winnipeg man says the damage left by Sunday night's thunderstorm was "overwhelming," after his vehicle rolled into the front yard of a nearby home.
Some power outages for roughly 4,000 Hydro customers could stretch into Tuesday
High winds and heavy rains led to downed power lines and trees, particularly in Winnipeg's Westwood and River Heights areas, Hydro spokesperson Peter Chura told CBC News on Monday morning.
Sometime during the storm, Darryl Gervais says the wind pushed his Pontiac Vibe, which rolled over into a nearby lawn on Lindsay Street in the River Heights area.
Gervais said he had just finished repairs on the vehicle and left it for his son to use right before the storm hit.
"It looked wonderful, and now it doesn't," he told CBC News on Monday. "The windows are smashed, the roof is crumpled, and there's a trail of parts along the lawn."
But Gervais is glad no one was hurt, saying if the vehicle had rolled another three metres, it would have hit a house.
"It's incredible, the force of the wind that can pick up a 3,000 pound vehicle," he said.
"Yesterday, I was working on it, figuring it would last another two years."

Preliminary numbers from Environment Canada show winds in the city reached 83 kilometres per hour on Sunday night, while 35 millimetres of rain hit Winnipeg overall and The Forks got nearly 70 millimetres.
Robyn Canicula, who lives nearby on Lindsay Street, says her family may be staying in a hotel for the next few days, after the storm damaged her home just before her children head back to school.
"We can't go in the backyard because there's a power line down," Canicula told CBC News on Monday. "Our trampoline's gone, our pergola's up in a tree down the road."
The storm left destruction all over the neigbourhood, including downed power lines and trees, as well as power lines that were cut in half, she said.
"It feels like we're in a movie. It's pretty scary."
Canicula is thankful the community has come together in light of the damage, she said.

"We've had a lot of neighbors reach out," she said. "Actually, somebody's been helping my husband put a tarp on our roof and our neighbour's roof, so it's been really nice, all the support we've been getting from the community."

items: What's open and closed this Labour Day in Manitoba

blocks.text: About 4,000 customers in Winnipeg were without power on Monday morning, Hydro's Chura said.

Although crews worked through the night to repair damage and restore power to some, people in areas that suffered severe damage should expect "extended outages today and likely into tomorrow," Chura said.
"We'll assess the damage and concentrate on the damage that's going to restore the most customers to power at once, and then work our way down from there," he said.
"There's more severe weather in the forecast, so that could complicate repairs and cause further hazards for people."
Hydro is urging the public to stay away from downed powerlines and to report them to 911, said Chura.
"And remember, a downed tree can also be hiding other hazards, so stay away from those as well."

articles.title: Province rejects calls to install rescue equipment at B.C. lakes, despite surge in drownings
articles.summary: So far this year, 42 people have drowned in B.C.

image.caption: Four friends who live in Squamish, including one lifeguard and another person who works near one of the lakes, are trying to make a difference and prevent drowning deaths. (Alanna Kelly/CBC)

blocks.text: British Columbia
So far this year, 42 people have drowned in B.C.
So far this year, 42 people have drowned in B.C.
After a deadly summer on the water in B.C., four Squamish friends are advocating for rescue equipment to be installed at provincial parks.
B.C. has recorded a spike in drownings, with 42 people dying so far this year.
There were 27 deaths in the same time frame last year, according to the B.C. and Yukon Lifesaving Society.
Lenea Grace, the executive director for the society, said the increase is alarming.
“We want to equip British Columbians to make safe choices when they're on the water,” Grace said.
In some of the deaths, Grace said, people were not wearing a life jacket.
“An average of over 40 per cent of drownings in B.C. involve non-use of a life jacket,” she said.
In late May, a couple died after falling from a paddleboard at Browning Lake near Squamish, at Murrin Provincial Park.
After the tragedy, four friends — Auni Dayton, Ella Henriques, Zoë Prescott and Zeia Dayton — came together and floated an idea of how they could help improve safety.
“I've always actually been passionate about policy, and I've always been interested in what someone can do as a citizen to speak to their government,” Henriques said.
Together, the group wrote a letter to the District of Squamish’s mayor and council back in July asking for improvements to be made to the local swimming lakes.

items: Body of 13-year-old girl recovered from B.C.'s Cultus Lake: RCMP

blocks.text: “We want to see life jacket-loaner systems, we want to see better signage, we want to see better swimming education,” Prescott said.
Henriques said they’d also like to see rescue buoys or rings near the waterfronts at the provincial lakes such as Alice Lake, Browning Lake and Cat Lake.
“It's really not that much, not costly at all, since each is like $200,” Henriques said.
District of Squamish Mayor Armand Hurford then wrote a letter to B.C.’s Ministry of Environment and Parks encouraging the safety initiatives.
“I really think that in those particular places, there’s not only a need but a responsibility,” Hurford said.
He believes the province has an obligation to ensure safety for people.
“It's important for those multi-jurisdictions to come together and to take actions that will address this,” Hurford said.
Both the mayor and the group of advocates have not heard back from the province.

In an email statement to CBC News, the Ministry of Environment and Parks said B.C. Parks does not provide life jackets or rescue stations in provincial parks and does not have an intention to change this practice.
“People recreating in provincial parks are expected to know how to safely conduct activities in parks, including swimming and other water-based activities,” states the ministry.
Having loaner life jackets that people can easily use, is a step that Grace feels could prevent deaths.
“I'm disappointed to hear this because these are steps that would make a considerable difference between life and death should a situation arise,” Grace said.
Lifesaving Society is hopeful Transport Canada would implement mandatory life jackets for adults on paddleboards.

items: Family identifies couple involved in paddleboarding accident near Squamish

blocks.text: “We continue to advocate and support this endeavour,” Grace said.
As for the group of four friends, they aren’t stopping spreading their message.
“The sooner this type of stuff gets installed, the sooner we prevent drownings and the one less person that has to drown,” Henriques said.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Alanna Kelly is a CBC News journalist based in Squamish, B.C., covering the Sea-to-Sky region, including Whistler, Pemberton and the Sunshine Coast. You can email story ideas to alanna.kelly@cbc.ca.

articles.title: Romualdez seeks continued hospital confinement amid plunder case
articles.summary: Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez on Monday sought the approval of the Sandiganbayan Third Division to grant him "continued hospital confinement" as he faces his plunder case.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 9:59pm
Former House Speaker Martin Romualdez on Monday sought the approval of the Sandiganbayan Third Division to grant him "continued hospital confinement" as he faces his plunder case.

The Office of the Ombudsman earlier filed a ₱7.4-billion plunder charge against Romualdez, former Ako Bicol party-list Rep. Zaldy Co, and their two co-accused over their alleged involvement in a kickback scheme on flood control projects.
A few hours later, the anti-graft court’s Third Division issued arrest warrants against them. Romualdez at that time was already confined at Cardinal Santos Medical Center in San Juan City.
A "24 Oras" report said Romualdez was read the warrant and his rights in the presence of his lawyer.

In a nine-page manifestation addressed to the Sandiganbayan, Romualdez said that he was admitted to the hospital on September 7, 2026, and cited a medical history concerning his cardiovascular health and brain condition.
In the document’s prayer, Romualdez requested the following to the Court:

items: Authorize the serving of any arrest warrant upon him at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center
Allow him to remain under continuous lawful custody at the hospital for as long as inpatient confinement remains necessary, until he is medically cleared for transfer
Approve the custody and security protocol he proposed
Note that his submission to any warrant does not constitute a waiver of his previous objections to the case

blocks.text: Under the former speaker’s suggested custody and security protocols, he proposed that he be permitted to complete his booking and custodial documentation upon the service of the warrant.
Other requests under the proposed protocols include, among others:

items: Continuous medical custody by Dr. Rosalio Torres and other responsible officers of the hospital designated by the Court
Round-the-clock security guards
Visitor restrictions and a visitor log
No departure from or transfer out of the hospital without the court’s approval
Arrangements for his required court appearances consistent with medical advice and court orders

blocks.text: Heart, brain condition
In his manifestation for hospital arrest, Romualdez cited his medical history, including the angioplasty surgery he underwent in October 2024 due to his coronary artery disease.
The document stated that since then, he has required continuing cardiac monitoring and treatment.

“He is currently confined due to the following: Hypertensive Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease, Unstable Angina, Coronary Artery Disease, S/P PCI (post percutaneous coronary intervention), Cerebrovascular Ischemic Disease, Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, Hypertension, Dyslipidemia, and Primary Hypothyroidism,” the motion read.
“... Accused previously underwent Angioplasty Surgery on 05 October 2024 due to Coronary Artery Disease, and has since required continuing cardiac monitoring and treatment,” it added.

The document noted that Romualdez’s current status, as reflected in his medical certificates, justifies the necessity of continuous inpatient care, warning of risks should his treatment be interrupted or if he be transferred.

His attending physician, Dr. Torres, pledged to immediately inform the court if Romualdez’s health changes significantly or if he becomes healthy enough to be cleared for transfer out of the hospital.
Shortly after police secured the former Speaker at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, he was placed under arrest and underwent the booking process in his hospital room.—LDF, GMA News

articles.title: Nathan Fielder teases Elizabeth Holmes documentary with eyebrow-raising trailer
articles.summary: Fielder's new film about Holmes, You Can See Everything, was made with documentarian and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim and centres on the weeks leading up to Holmes's incarceration in 2023.

image.caption: Nathan Fielder, creator and executive producer of the television series The Rehearsal, arrives at the 86th annual Peabody Awards on Sunday, May 31, 2026, at the Beverly Wilshire in Beverly Hills, Calif. (Chris Pizzello/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Fielder's new film about Holmes, You Can See Everything, was made with documentarian and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim and centres on the weeks leading up to Holmes's incarceration in 2023.
Documentary centres on weeks leading up to Holmes's incarceration following 2022 Theranos fraud conviction
If you were wondering what possible antics Nathan Fielder has been up to after watching the latest season of The Rehearsal, we have your answer.

The Vancouver-born comedian, writer and director released a teaser late Sunday for his next project, a documentary about Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes who was famously convicted of fraud in 2022 after her company claimed to have created a type of blood testing that could screen for hundreds of diseases with small amounts of blood.
Fielder's film, titled You Can See Everything, was made with documentarian and filmmaker Lance Oppenheim and centres on the weeks leading up to Holmes's incarceration in 2023.
Oppenheim's previous works include Spermworld (2024), an FX-produced doc about sperm donors and Some Kind of Heaven (2020) about a Florida retirement community.

items: Theranos's Elizabeth Holmes sentenced to more than 11 years in federal prison

blocks.text: Fielder grew to fame with Nathan For You, a series on Comedy Central in which he gives horrible business advice to entrepreneurs. Previously he won (and baffled) Canadian hearts and minds with his appearances on CBC's This Hour Has 22 Minutes, in field segments titled "Nathan On Your Side" in 2008 and 2009.
You Can See Everything is being distributed by Gen Z favourite A24. The trailer features the company's signature high-saturation colour grading and overall eeriness.

It includes a roughly-one minute close-up conversation between Holmes and Fielder. The two intensely gaze at each other, as Holmes says, "Why would I deceive you? There's no — there's no reason for me to do that."
A long-ish silence follows and Fielder — with an incredulous expression on his face — says, "You're being real right now?"

The trailer was released in conjunction with a surprise screening Sunday at the Telluride Film Festival in Colorado. Reviews haven't yet surfaced from the screening, several critics posted their superlative-filled reactions to social media.

Film director Daniel Howat wrote on X after the screening that You Can See Everything "is maybe the most hysterical, shocking, insane documentary I’ve ever seen. Endlessly thought-provoking ... A work of genius."

Los Angeles-based music producer Erik Nordgren called it "easily the best film of the year for me, arguably on my best of the decade list. It turns from an uneasy-as-hell doc into something structurally, stylistically, and formally even more shocking. Like nothing I’ve ever seen."

The exchange harkens back to another uncomfortable, lesser-known interview Fielder conducted on This Hour Has 22 Minutes with former CBC president Hubert T. Lacroix in 2008. The two sit across from each other and Lacroix is put on the spot when he says he's a fan of Fielder's work but struggles to come up with any examples.
You Can See Everything is set to release in theatres next month.
ABOUT THE AUTHOR
Verity is a reporter for CBC in Montreal. She previously worked for the Globe and Mail, Toronto Star and the New Brunswick Telegraph-Journal.

articles.title: House panel eyes restoring funds to DepEd programs cut from 2027 NEP
articles.summary: The House Committee on Appropriations is considering restoring funding for several DepEd programs that were cut or not included in the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP).

blocks.text: The House Committee on Appropriations is considering restoring funding for several Department of Education (DepEd) programs that were cut or not included in the proposed 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), with committee chairperson Mikaela Suansing asking the agency to submit a prioritized list of programs for possible augmentation.

Suansing raised the issue during the committee’s deliberations on DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget on Monday, noting that while the department’s overall proposed budget for next year is higher by ₱41.3 billion than this year's budget, much of the increase is set to go to Personnel Services.

“So just extrapolating from there, we see that there was a P16-billion cut. There was a P16-billion cut in the other programs, the other components, and MOOE [Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses], capital outlay," she said.
She added that the affected programs included special needs education, school-based feeding, ARAL and mental health, among others.
Suansing said that Congress had previously augmented several of these programs during the last budget cycle.
“So siguro po titignan natin [perhaps we will look at] which among the programs which comprise the P16-billion decrease in MOOE and capital outlay, we can consider for augmentation.”
House asks: What happens if funding isn’t restored?
Suansing asked Angara to explain the consequences if the funding for the affected programs remained at the levels proposed in the 2027 NEP.
“What would happen if we’re unable to restore the funding for these particular programs?” she asked.
Angara said the impact would be particularly felt in the School-Based Feeding Program.
The 2027 NEP allocation is back at around ₱11 billion, compared with the roughly ₱26 billion Congress provided for the program in the 2026 GAA.
Angara said the lower allocation would mean a shorter feeding cycle.
“So right now you’re looking at 120 days instead of 180 days, which is the whole school year…” he said.
He said children who stop receiving meals before the end of the school year could fall back into the same problem the program seeks to address.
“…pag hindi natin pinakain for the remainder of the school year, babalik din sila. So in a way, parang you go forward, but you go back.”
(…if we don’t feed them for the remainder of the school year, they will return to the same condition. So in a way, you move forward, but then you go back.)
Angara also said the lower allocation would mean DepEd could not provide universal feeding for Grade 1.
“And the second is we won’t have universal feeding for Grade 1. So we’ll have it for Kinder, but not for Grade 1,” he said.
The department would also have less room to expand its central kitchens and provide more hot meals.
DepEd reports 45.8% utilization of 2026 feeding funds

Suansing also asked about DepEd’s ability to absorb the larger ₱26-billion feeding allocation in the 2026 GAA, recalling concerns about whether there would be enough milk suppliers and kitchens to implement the program.
Angara said the program currently had a 45.8% utilization rate, but explained that school-based feeding is tied to the school calendar and some payments carry over to the following year.
He said utilization had reached 90% in 2025 and 81% in 2024, indicating an improvement in the department’s ability to spend the funds.
Suansing said the figures suggested DepEd was on track to utilize the 2026 allocation.
ARAL faces zero funding in 2027 NEP
Suansing also pressed Angara on the ARAL program, recalling that Congress had funded the program during the previous budget cycle.
She asked how many students would be excluded if funding for ARAL were not restored.
“That would be all, but I think we would be forced to reallocate within the current budget," said Angara.
He said DepEd could potentially take money from other existing needs to keep the program running as he described ARAL as a potential “game changer” for learners who are falling behind.

DepEd’s supplemental budget request separately seeks funding for programs not covered or insufficiently funded in the 2027 NEP, including its learning recovery priorities. The department is seeking a total of ₱145.19 billion in supplemental funding.
Suansing said SpEd, along with other inclusive education programs, was among the areas Congress wanted to strengthen.
Angara said the department had also requested additional funding for special needs education, including personnel, facilities, equipment and program support.
The 2027 supplemental request includes ₱541.57 million for SPED, as well as funding for Madrasah, Indigenous Peoples education and multigrade education.
Mental health was likewise among the programs identified by lawmakers for possible augmentation.
The supplemental request includes funding for mental health and guidance services, school counselor associates and other learner support programs.
DepEd asked to re-prioritize ₱145B supplemental request
With DepEd seeking ₱145.19 billion in additional funding, Suansing acknowledged the difficulty of accommodating the entire request given the government’s fiscal space.
She asked Angara to submit a more streamlined and prioritized list of requests.

Suansing also asked DepEd to submit the re-prioritized list by Wednesday noon, citing the House’s upcoming plenary schedule and the chamber’s process of reviewing institutional budget requests through its Budget Amendment Review Subcommittee.
She nevertheless told DepEd that the committee would seek to accommodate its requests.
Earlier, Appropriations Vice Chair Maria Carmen Zamora said the committee had seen broad support from lawmakers for increasing, not cutting, DepEd’s proposed budget.

“Out of the 34 members who asked questions, I have not heard any single member who posed for the cut of the budget, but instead all of these 34, from the minority and majority, have proposed for the increase of the proposed budget," she said.
Zamora said lawmakers highlighted SNED, inclusive resource center construction, school-based feeding, computerization, school building, ARAL and mental health programs, among others.

DepEd’s proposed FY 2027 budget is ₱973.4 billion for the department proper, while its six attached agencies have a combined proposed allocation of about ₱2.56 billion, bringing the total to around ₱975.96 billion.

The department’s Personnel Services allocation is proposed to increase by 8.64% to ₱766.74 billion, while MOOE would decrease by 15.94% to ₱174.32 billion and Capital Outlay by 67.49% to ₱32.34 billion.
DepEd is seeking ₱145.19 billion in supplemental funding to address gaps in learning recovery, personnel, school infrastructure, learner support and inclusive education.
The committee subsequently terminated its deliberations on the proposed FY 2027 DepEd budget under House Bill No. 10858, including its attached agencies. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: Pakistan: Can creating new provinces fix governance?
articles.summary: Pakistanis broadly agree that the country needs more responsive and effective government, but many question whether simply creating more provinces is the solution.

image.caption: Supporters of creating more provinces say Pakistan's four existing provinces have become too large and centralized [FILE: April 2026]Image: Akhtar Soomro/REUTERS

blocks.text: A politically sensitive debate has reignited in Pakistan over whether its four-province system can effectively govern a country of around 260 million people.

Ahsan Iqbal, minister for planning and development, recently called for a national political debate on administrative reform. He proposed creating 12 to 15 new provinces or setting up 160 empowered district governments to improve governance and the delivery of public services.
Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who first raised the idea of an administrative "reset" in July, said on Saturday that any new administrative units should be created with public support.
Defense Minister Khawaja Asif, meanwhile, has called for greater decentralization and devolution of power to the grassroots.
Despite the growing calls to create new provinces, no formal decision has been taken.
Even within the ruling coalition, there is disagreement over how and when such reforms should be pursued.
There are also questions about whether creating smaller provinces improves governance, or whether devolving power directly to local governments would be more effective.
Basmati rice: India, Pakistan and the EU dispute
More provinces, better governance?
Pakistanis broadly agree that the country needs more responsive and effective government, but many question whether creating more provinces is the solution.

"Smaller provinces are not a substitute for empowered local governments. Even with smaller provinces, you will still need empowered local governments to make the system effective and improve service delivery to the people," Miftah Ismail, a former finance minister and economist, told DW.
Supporters of creating more provinces argue that Pakistan's four existing provinces — Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan — have become too large and overly centralized.
Iqbal, the planning minister, has argued that the existing system has not delivered adequate improvements in health, education, and other social services.
Interior Minister Naqvi, on the other hand, has called for an administrative structure that is better suited to Pakistan's growing population.
But there is disagreement over the solution.

"Without effective local governments, whether there is one province or 25, decision-making will remain centralized at the provincial level," Abid Qaiyum Suleri, executive director of the Sustainable Development Policy Institute, an Islamabad-based think tank, told DW.

He said any proposal for new provinces or administrative units should be assessed against potential improvements in local tax collection and the costs of creating new provincial institutions, including secretariats, assemblies, and bureaucracies.
Suleri stressed that it should also be examined whether such changes would deliver justice and public services more effectively.
Can Pakistan still help end the US-Iran war?
Altering the political balance

"Pakistan's history suggests that empowering local governments is a better choice in terms of governance and provision of services," Muhammad Shoaib, a political scientist and assistant professor at Quaid-i-Azam University in Islamabad, told DW.
The debate, therefore, is not simply about how many provinces Pakistan should have, but whether creating smaller units would actually make the government more responsive to citizens.
Creating new provinces could also affect the political balance in the country.
New provinces would mean new governments and assemblies, while potentially changing political representation and the distribution of federal resources.
Any attempt to redraw boundaries could also reopen disputes over water, taxation, and natural resources.

The political resistance is already tangible. Sindh's provincial assembly has opposed creating new provinces or administrative units in the province, while political groups have warned against dividing existing territories.
Why Pakistan may be too reliant on EU trade
A risky strategy?
Shoaib said dividing resources would present a major challenge, even if all provinces were reorganized at the same time.
"Even if all provinces are divided simultaneously, the division of resources like finances, water, and jobs, and special privileges for territories within provinces will be a challenge," he said.
"Challenges like these require lengthy negotiations and compromises for political consensus," he added.
The issue is therefore not only about administrative efficiency, as redrawing provincial boundaries could also redistribute political and economic power.
Ismail believes redrawing provincial boundaries would be risky, particularly in Sindh.
He said empowering existing local governments within current provincial boundaries would be a safer option.

"We can learn from the US and the southern states of India, where empowered small administrative units, while competing with each other, are more responsive to citizens and deliver better services," Ismail said.

Shoaib said Pakistan could also learn from other countries, particularly democratic systems that have empowered local governments and taken time to work through the division of large states into smaller units.
"In Pakistan's case, the risk of resistance and perpetual resentment is real. A partially finished division will aggravate existing ethnic tensions," he said.
For Pakistan, the debate is therefore about more than whether the country should have four provinces or 12 or 15.

It is about whether changing the administrative map can actually bring power, resources, and accountability closer to its people, and whether such a transformation can be achieved without creating new political and ethnic tensions.

articles.title: EU's Von der Leyen pledges $232 million Greenland investment
articles.summary: The EU is preparing a major investment package and closer political ties with the Danish Arctic territory amid Donald Trump's demand for greater US control of the mineral-rich island.

image.caption: Von der Leyen (right) said the visit was about further cementing a unique partnership with the regionImage: Mads Claus Rasmussen/Ritzau Scanpix/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen has pledged €200 million ($232 million) investment package for Greenland as the EU seeks closer relations with the Arctic territory.

Von der Leyen has been visiting Nuuk, the capital of thje Danish autonomous island, for the past two days where she met with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenlandic counterpart Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
Von der Leyen's visit comes after threats of US annexation earlier this year by President Donald Trump.
What von der Leyen said?
"Territorial integrity sovereignty, the inviolability of borders, these are fundamental principles of international law," von der Leyen told a joint press conference.
The EU chief announced the "EU-Greenland Partnership Package," focusing on three priorities: connectivity, clean energy and critical raw materials.
"This is 200 million euros of new investments for Greenland for this year and the next," von der Leyen said.
She emphasized that "Greenland's future is for the people of Greenland and Denmark to decide, no one else."
The European Commission head arrived in Nuuk on Sunday in a show of support for Greenland and Denmark, and was received by Nielsen and Frederiksen.

"We’re deepening our cooperation across the board. Connectivity, clean energy, critical raw materials. And of course, more opportunities for the people of Greenland," Von der Leyen said in a post on X.
What does the EU investment package include?
The EU package is expected to include hundreds of millions of euros in investment in:

items: critical minerals
satellite communications
renewable energy

blocks.text: Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen described the visit as an opportunity to deepen the territory's "close friendship and good partnership" with the EU.
The largely autonomous Greenland left the EU in 1985, although its population of about 57,000 are EU citizens through Danish citizenship.
Why is Trump demanding 'total access' over Greenland?

Von der Leyen's visit comes as the Arctic gains strategic importance for the US, Russia, China and Europe, with melting sea ice opening new shipping routes and increasing access to the region's mineral resources.

Trump has repeatedly stated that the US "needs" Greenland for its "national security," pointing to his claims — without providing evidence — that the island is "covered with Chinese and Russian ships all over the place."
Trump has maintained that Denmark cannot adequately defend the island against China and Russia.

His campaign bid to gain "total access" to the Danish territory has strained US-European relations and raised tensions within NATO as both Greenland and the Danish government have rejected Trump's demands.
Greenland's ice-covered minerals: No easy option

articles.title: House panel directs Judiciary to submit items that need addt'l funding
articles.summary: The House Committee on Appropriations on Monday asked the Supreme Court (SC) and other courts to submit a list of items that need additional funding.

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 9:33pm
The House Committee on Appropriations on Monday asked the Supreme Court (SC) and other courts to submit a list of items that need additional funding.
During its budget hearing, the Judiciary said it is requesting an augmentation of P5.344 billion from its original budget proposal of P86.271 billion.

“We ask the SC and other courts, of course the Sandiganbayan, Court of Tax Appeals, and the Court of Appeals to submit what you think should be augmented,” Committee Vice Chairperson Rufus Rodriguez said.
Meanwhile, Committee Chairperson Mikaela Suansing asked the courts to submit the requested documents by Wednesday.
Construction of Halls of Justice

According to Court Administrator Ma. Theresa Gomez-Estosta, the judiciary needs an additional funding of P4.541 billion for the construction of Halls of Justice (HOJ) in Cebu City and P500 million for Cagayan de Oro City.
The judiciary also seeks an additional P303 million for the hazard pay of its sheriffs, Gomez-Estosta said.
Meanwhile, Vice Chairperson John Cagas and Iloilo City Representative Julienne Baronda called on the SC to construct a Hall of Justice in Davao del Sur and Iloilo City, respectively.

“Okay na sa amin P150 million. One storey lang. Ayaw namin ng mataas na building dahil sa lindol. Na-trauma ‘yung mga tao doon. Ayaw na nila ng mataataas— kasi maraming fault line sa amin,” Cagas said.

(P150 million is enough for us. Just one storey. We don’t want a tall building because of earthquakes. The people there were traumatized. They no longer want tall buildings — because there are many fault lines in our area.)
Gomez-Estosta and SC Associate Justice Raul VIllanueva assured the panel that the SC will realign its funds for the construction.
For her part, Baronda said that the HOJ in Iloilo was opened in 1992.
“In 2012, nagkaroon ng major retrofitting ang Hall of Justice and in 2025, it was discussed na unsafe for you to stay there. But until now, you are still occupying the Hall of Justice,” she said.
(In 2012, there was major retrofitting of the Hall of Justice, and in 2025, it was discussed that it was unsafe for you to stay there. But until now, you are still occupying the Hall of Justice.)
Assistant Minority Leader Representative Robert Nazal said he believes that the judiciary has demonstrated that additional resources can be put to use.
“On the part of the minority, we support an adequate increase in the judiciary’s budget,” he said.
Rodriguez then made the motion to terminate the hearing on the judiciary’s budget. — BAP, GMA News

articles.title: Zero budget for new teachers in 2027 proposed DepEd budget
articles.summary: The Department of Education (DepEd) received zero budget for the hiring of new teachers in 2027. DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara told the House Committee on Appropriations that for next year, "the…

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 9:31pm
The Department of Education (DepEd) received zero budget for the hiring of new teachers in 2027.
DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara told the House Committee on Appropriations that for next year, "the shortage is 14,274 teachers, costing around P4.29 billion."
But Angara explained that DepEd will be hiring new teachers this year, more than the usual number.
"We got 32,000 this year, which is above the average hiring, your honor, I think, which averages around 20,000," he said.
The promotion of qualified teachers is also facing a backlog.

"For 2026, there is a P6 billion budget given by Congress, and this is enough to promote 82,000 of our teachers and school heads. In 2027, there is a P12 billion budget, and this should answer for the promotions of 135,000 school heads," the Education chief said.
However, he added that "there are about 100,000 still waiting and entitled to the promotions" who are still waiting for available funding.
House Committee on Appropriations head Rep. Mikaela Suansing gave the DepEd until Wednesday to submit a streamlined and rationalized "reprioritized list."
Other personnel needs

Aside from the additional teachers, DepEd’s proposed 2027 budget in the National Expenditure Program (NEP) includes ₱801.5 million for the hiring of 1,800 school counselor associates and 221 schools division office counselors.
The department said its broader supplemental personnel request is intended to provide teachers with additional support so they can focus on teaching.

On Monday, DepEd presented a proposed P975.96-billion budget for fiscal year 2027, including allocations for its attached agencies, before the House panel, according to the department’s press release.
The department is seeking an additional P145.19 billion for critical programs not funded under the 2027 NEP.

Under the proposed NEP allocation, Personnel Services would rise 8.64% to P766.74 billion, while Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) would decline 15.94% to P174.32 billion and Capital Outlay would fall 67.49% to P32.34 billion. —With Sherylin Untalan/LDF, GMA News

articles.title: LTO revokes license of driver of Torre’s vehicle over plate misuse
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Office (LTO) on Monday announced that it had revoked the license of the driver of the vehicle owned by Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA)…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Land Transportation Office (LTO) on Monday announced that it had revoked the license of the driver of the vehicle owned by Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) General Manager Nicolas Torre III.
A video-recorded incident showed the driver operating the vehicle bearing MMDA markings and identifiers, including a body number, siren, and blinker.
“However, an LTO verification found that the vehicle’s license plate did not match its records and that the SUV was registered as a private vehicle,” the LTO said.

A show cause order was issued against the driver on Aug. 28, and in a Sept. 4 order, the LTO imposed a one-year suspension of his driver’s license after declaring him an “Improper Person to Operate a Motor Vehicle.”
But the investigation found that the same driver was also involved in another incident involving the same vehicle, prompting the LTO to issue another show cause order.
The LTO confirmed that the driver involved in the first incident was also operating the vehicle when the second incident occurred.
The incidents pointed to repeated violations and misrepresentation involving the vehicle’s use and unauthorized markings and identifiers.
“As a result, the LTO declared the driver an ‘Improper Person to Operate a Motor Vehicle’ and ultimately revoked his driver’s license,” the LTO said.
Meanwhile, the MMDA-marked SUV remains impounded at the LTO Central Office.
LTO chief and Assistant Secretary Markus Lacanilao said, “Regardless of your rank, position or office, if you violate traffic laws, I will not let it pass.”
“We in government clearly understand the law. Let us follow it, do what is right and be responsible on the road,” he pointed out. /mcm

articles.title: Marcos calls for job-focused education amid skills shortages
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Monday called on schools and businesses to ensure that education and training programs equip Filipinos with skills that match the needs of a…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr. on Monday called on schools and businesses to ensure that education and training programs equip Filipinos with skills that match the needs of a changing labor market.
He said this during his visit to Lipa-Malvar Estate, Batangas State University (BSU) LIMA Campus, in Malvar and Lipa City, Batangas.
His visit also marks the 1st Anniversary of JERA-Aboitiz Power Global Technical Center of Excellence (GTCOE).

“Our people deserve the skills that allow them to find meaningful work, build careers, and contribute to the growth of our economy and our country. At the same time, education should also address the needs of our industries and demands of our society,” Marcos said.
“The challenge before us is clear: As our industries evolve, we must ensure that our people are equipped to grow with them,” he also said.

Marcos cited a 2021 study by the Asian Development Bank, which revealed that around a third of college graduates are employed in jobs that are designed specifically for those with non-college education.
The same study said two-thirds of technical-vocational education and training graduates are employed in occupations unrelated to the expected outcomes of their training programs.
Additionally, the labor force surveys show the prevalence of hard-to-fill occupations, which Marcos said signals a skills shortage.
“These figures call on us to bring education and training closer to the needs of our industries, and to better prepare our people for the opportunities that lay ahead,” he said.

The BSU LIMA Campus was established on June 19, 2025, in partnership with Aboitiz Infracapital Economic Estates, which donated 10 hectares of land within the LIMA Estate to the BSU for the development of its new engineering and technology campus.

The GTCOE, meanwhile, which celebrates its first anniversary, is a technical training facility for engineers and technical professionals in the power sector located at the LIMA Commercial Center in the LIMA estate. /gsg

articles.title: Loren Legarda praises enactment of stronger free college law
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — More students from poor families can now stay in school and finish their education, Sen. Loren Legarda said as she welcomed on Monday the enactment of Republic Act No. 12325,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — More students from poor families can now stay in school and finish their education, Sen. Loren Legarda said as she welcomed on Monday the enactment of Republic Act No. 12325, which strengthens the Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education.

The new law, signed by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Sept. 4, improves the tertiary education subsidy (TES) by directing assistance more deliberately toward the poorest students and recognizing that the cost of education goes far beyond tuition.

“It’s not enough that tuition is free if students have no money for fare to go to school and buy books, and then are short of money to buy food, or are forced to stop to help their families. Free college must mean that a student has a real chance not only to enroll, but to stay in school and graduate,” Legarda said in a mix of Filipino and English in a statement issued on Monday.
More focus on poor students

Legarda principally sponsored and authored Senate Bill No. 1894, which strengthened Republic Act No. 10931 by making student assistance more responsive to the actual financial burden of pursuing college or technical-vocational education.

Among its key reforms is focusing the subsidy more on students who need government assistance most, particularly senior high school graduates from Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) households who are admitted to qualified higher education or technical-vocational institutions.

The reform addresses a significant gap identified by the Second Congressional Commission on Education (Edcom II). Legarda now serves as an Edcom II commissioner, previously serving as its co-chairperson. She was also the chairperson of the Senate Committee on Higher, Technical, and Vocational Education

As Legarda points out, the share of TES beneficiaries from the poorest households fell from 70.73 percent in 2018 to 22.89 percent in 2022. Of 384,388 senior high school graduates from 4Ps households, only 4,746, or 1.23 percent, received TES as first-year beneficiaries in academic year 2024–2025.

“The data is clear. Many youths who should get aid first don’t benefit from it. We strengthened the system to make sure that more families in need will get the opportunity to let their children finish. We can’t describe an opportunity as universal if the poorest are the ones who get aid last,” Legarda said.
Regular subsidy reviews
The new law also provides for regular reviews of TES amounts so that it can respond to changes in the actual cost of education.

To make tertiary education more inclusive, state universities and colleges, local universities and colleges, and state-run technical-vocational institutions are also required to adopt Equity and Inclusion Plans.
This aims to remove barriers faced by persons with disabilities, students from geographically isolated and disadvantaged areas, indigenous peoples, and learners from other disadvantaged backgrounds.

The law also establishes the Private Education Assistance Program, which will support qualified students who need financial assistance in private higher education institutions and technical-vocational schools.

Legarda pointed out that the law advances a principle she had been consistently pushing in education policy — that government must look beyond how many students enter school and focus on whether they are actually able to finish.

“We hope to ensure that no Filipino youth will lose the opportunity to get a quality education just because their families lack money. The lack of money should not be a reason for their education to be cut short and their dreams blocked,” she said. /atm

articles.title: Ilocos Sur town probes dredging near its waters
articles.summary: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The municipal government of Sta. Lucia said it would not tolerate unauthorized or environmentally harmful dredging within its jurisdiction, citing the need to protect…

blocks.text: SAN ILDEFONSO, Ilocos Sur — The municipal government of Sta. Lucia said it would not tolerate unauthorized or environmentally harmful dredging within its jurisdiction, citing the need to protect marine ecosystems and the livelihoods of coastal communities.

The statement came after municipal officials inspected a dredging activity off Barangay Nangalisan on Monday, Sept. 7, to determine whether the operation falls within Sta. Lucia’s territorial waters and assess its possible environmental impact.
The initial on-site assessment showed that the dredging site was about 1,933 meters from the identified municipal boundary toward Sabangan, an area under neighboring Sta. Cruz town.

Mayor Joseph Simon Valdez, Vice Mayor Eduardo Toquero, members of the Sangguniang Bayan, barangay officials and representatives from the Municipal Engineering and Assessor’s offices joined the inspection, along with personnel from the police and Bureau of Fire Protection.

The local government said the measurement and site inspection form part of its continuing verification of the dredging operation’s exact location in relation to the boundaries of Sta. Lucia and Sta. Cruz.
Officials also documented conditions in the area and assessed the possible effects of the dredging on the coastal environment.
The municipal government said it would coordinate with concerned government agencies to determine whether the operation complies with environmental laws and other regulations. /mcm

articles.title: Eastern Visayas power coops warn of outages amid grid alert
articles.summary: TACLOBAN CITY — Electric cooperatives in Eastern Visayas warned consumers Monday, Sept. 7, of possible power interruptions as the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) placed the…

blocks.text: TACLOBAN CITY — Electric cooperatives in Eastern Visayas warned consumers Monday, Sept. 7, of possible power interruptions as the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines (NGCP) placed the Visayas grid under red and yellow alerts due to tight power supply.
NGCP said it may implement Manual Load Dropping (MLD) from 4 p.m. to 9 p.m. in areas served by the following distribution utilities and electric cooperatives:

items: Leyte Electric Cooperative II (Leyeco II)
Southern Leyte Electric Cooperative (Soleco)
Don Orestes Romualdez Electric Cooperative Inc. (Dorelco)
Leyeco III
Leyeco IV
Leyeco V
Eastern Samar Electric Cooperative (Esamelco)
Biliran Electric Cooperative (Bileco)
Northern Samar Electric Cooperative (Norsamelco)
Samar I Electric Cooperative (Samelco I)
Samar II Electric Cooperative (Samelco II)

blocks.text: About one million member-consumers are served by these distribution utilities across the region.
The possible power interruptions are intended to help protect the stability of the power grid amid limited generation and power imports from Mindanao, NGCP said.
The Visayas grid was placed under red alert from 6 p.m. to 7 p.m. and yellow alert from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m. and 7 p.m. to 9 p.m.
NGCP reported available capacity of 2,530 megawatts (MW) against a projected peak demand of 2,508 MW, leaving only a slim reserve.

It attributed the tight supply situation to the unavailability of the large coal-fired plants TVI 1 and PEDC 3, the 146.2-MW derating of THVI 2 due to a main steam problem, and limited power imports from Mindanao.
Eight power plants were on forced outage, while 15 others were operating at reduced capacity, resulting in a total of 818.9 MW of unavailable capacity.
NGCP said the MLD schedule may still be canceled if system conditions improve, such as when actual electricity demand falls below projections.

A red alert means available supply is insufficient to meet demand and the grid’s regulating requirement, while a yellow alert indicates that the operating margin is insufficient to meet the grid’s contingency requirement.
NGCP urged consumers to use electricity prudently, particularly during peak hours. /mcm

articles.title: Manila Water eyes completing San Juan Reservoir by end of 2026
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — As climate-related challenges and natural hazards become more frequent and severe, Manila Water is strengthening the resilience of its water supply infrastructure through the…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — As climate-related challenges and natural hazards become more frequent and severe, Manila Water is strengthening the resilience of its water supply infrastructure through the ongoing construction of the new San Juan Reservoir, a critical facility designed to withstand major earthquakes and support reliable water service for decades to come.

Targeted for completion by the end of 2026, the new 56-million-liter (ML) reservoir will replace the existing San Juan Reservoir and serve as a more robust and resilient water storage facility for communities in Metro Manila. Designed in accordance with modern engineering standards, the new reservoir incorporates upgraded structural, electrical, instrumentation, and mechanical systems that will help ensure uninterrupted service even in the face of increasing environmental and seismic risks.

The project forms part of Manila Water’s continuing investments to modernize and future-proof its water infrastructure amid growing challenges posed by urbanization, extreme weather events, and natural disasters.
The replacement project was pursued following extensive structural assessments of the existing San Juan Reservoir, which was originally constructed in 1968.

Engineering studies conducted by DCCD Engineering Corporation in 2011 and 2016 identified significant deterioration in the facility’s roof slab and walls resulting from decades of service. The assessments also indicated a high risk of structural failure during major seismic events, including a potential 7.2-magnitude earthquake.

In addition, the reservoir’s top slab had undergone several repairs due to holes and other defects that could potentially compromise the quality and safety of stored water supplying the San Juan Pumping Station.
Recognizing the need to enhance the long-term reliability and disaster resilience of the facility, Manila Water moved forward with the replacement of the aging reservoir.

With a total project cost of more than ₱970 million, the undertaking covers the demolition of the existing reservoir and the design and construction of the new 56-ML facility, including all associated electrical, instrumentation, mechanical, and site development works.
As of July 2026, construction progress has reached 84 percent, with work continuing toward the project’s targeted completion by the end of the year.

Once operational, the new San Juan Reservoir will strengthen the reliability of water supply service while providing greater resilience against earthquakes and other hazards that could affect critical water infrastructure.

“By investing in more resilient facilities, such as the San Juan Reservoir, we are enhancing our ability to continue delivering safe, reliable, and uninterrupted water service to the communities we serve, even during disruptive events,” Manila Water Corporate Communications Group Head Dittie Galang said.

The new San Juan Reservoir underscores Manila Water’s commitment to building infrastructure that not only meets growing water demand but also strengthens the resilience of the East Zone’s water supply system in an increasingly hazard-prone environment.

articles.title: LOOK: Martin Romualdez undergoes booking procedure in hospital room
articles.summary: Officers of the Philippine National Police served the warrant of arrest on former Speaker Martin Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after…

blocks.text: Published September 7, 2026 9:28pm

Officers of the Philippine National Police served the warrant of arrest on former Speaker Martin Romualdez at the Cardinal Santos Medical Center, where he was taken on Monday afternoon after suffering a cardiovascular event, unstable blood pressure, and an anxiety attack.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division issued the warrant of arrest following the filing of plunder charges against Romualdez, former congressman Zaldy Co, and two others.
One photo from the room showed Criminal Investigation and Detection Group chief Police Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico II reading the Leyte congressman his rights.
Another photo showed police officers taking Romualdez's fingerprints, according to booking procedures.
Romualdez had an orange shirt for persons deprived of liberty draped across his chest during the booking process.
Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla said a lawyer was with Romualdez when the latter received the warrant of arrest.
A lawyer for Romualdez said he would face all allegations against him in connection with his alleged links to the kickback scheme involving the flood control mess.

“We respect the courts and the legal process. Representative Ferdinand Martin G. Romualdez will face the allegations against him in accordance with law,” Atty. Ade Fajardo, counsel of Romualdez, said in a statement.

“We recognize the public interest surrounding this case. But ultimately, criminal liability must be determined by the evidence presented in court, under the rules and safeguards of our justice system,” he added.
He also said that Romualdez, a cousin of President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos, Jr., only asked for a fair shake.
P7.4B plunder charge

The Office of the Ombudsman on Monday filed a P7.4-billion plunder charge against Romualdez, former House appropriations panel chairperson Zaldy Co of Ako Bicol party-list, Joselyn Tragua Serenio, who is the personal assistant of Romualdez, and Felicito Cristobal Guevarra, president of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corporation.

“By repeatedly receiving, directly or indirectly, on at least 15 occasions, commissions, shares, percentages. kickbacks, "commitments." and/or other pecuniary benefits aggregating at least P7.4 billion by reason or on account of the respective public offices and positions of Romualdez and Co, including monies derived from contractors, persons and entities with interests in flood control, infrastructure and/or other government projects funded under the General Appropriations Acts for fiscal years 2022 to 2025, which monies were delivered to properties owned by, occupied by, or associated with Romualdez and received by Serenio and other persons acting for and in his behalf,” the criminal information read.
The Sandiganbayan Third Division hours later on Monday issued warrants of arrest against them.

"The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged," the Third Division said.

"Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested," it added.
Remulla said the hospital arrest was not a "permanent situation" for the former Speaker.
"But we assure you, we assure you, he cannot hide behind his wealth," Remulla said. –NB, GMA News

articles.title: Sara Duterte trial: Ridon says senator-judges aren’t being influenced
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said Monday that senator-judges will decide Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment case based solely on evidence,…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — House prosecutor and Bicol Saro party-list Rep. Terry Ridon said Monday that senator-judges will decide Vice President Sara Duterte’s impeachment case based solely on evidence, rejecting her claim that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. controls the Senate.
Ridon made the pronouncement after Duterte earlier issued a statement claiming that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. controls the Senate, court judges, the police, and fiscal matters.
“We have high regard for our senator-judges: We trust that they will make decisions based solely on evidence,” he said.
“They are not influenced by anyone, and contrary to the Vice President’s view, they are not controlled by anyone,” he added.
Duterte is currently facing the Senate impeachment court amid allegations of misusing confidential funds, unexplained wealth, bribery, and grave threats.

Much like in the impeachment complaint against her, Duterte was also recently ordered arrested by the Quezon City Regional Trial Court on Friday for three counts of grave threats stemming from alleged threats she made during a November 2024 virtual press conference against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., First Lady Liza Araneta-Marcos, and then-House Speaker and presidential cousin Martin Romualdez.
She has since posted bail of P120,000 for each count. /mcm

articles.summary: MABALACAT CITY — The police arrested four men for transporting some an estimated P48,955,500 worth of suspected smuggled cigarettes in Barangay Cacutud here shortly after midnight on Monday. In a…

blocks.text: MABALACAT CITY — The police arrested four men for transporting some an estimated P48,955,500 worth of suspected smuggled cigarettes in Barangay Cacutud here shortly after midnight on Monday.
In a statement, the Police Regional Office 3 (PRO3) said the operation which resulted in the arrest was carried out after several days of surveillance operations.
Authorities had received information that a truck was being used to transport and store cases of suspected illicit cigarettes at a secluded location in the city.

At around 12:30 a.m., operatives from the Regional Special Operations Group-Regional Intelligence Division 3, Mabalacat City Police Station, and Criminal Investigation and Detection Group Regional Field Unit 3 successfully intercepted the target truck and arrested its driver and three companions.

“A search of the truck led to the discovery of 759 master cases of ‘Modern’ cigarettes — 329 master cases of red packs and 430 master cases of blue packs. The products were observed to have no Bureau of Internal Revenue tax stamps and remain subject to further examination and verification,” the PRO3 said.

PRO3 Director Brig. Gen. Jess Mendez said the impact of the operation went beyond the amount of contraband seized, noting that illicit trade deprives the government of potential revenues that could support public services, puts legitimate businesses at a disadvantage, and allows illegal trade networks to profit at the expense of lawful commerce.
“Keeping these products off the market helps protect consumers, businesses, and the local economy,” he added.
The PRO3 said the recovered items were inventoried in the presence of the arrested individuals and a barangay official.
Alternative recording devices were also used during the operation in accordance with existing procedures.
The four arrested individuals and the recovered evidence were brought to the police regional camp for documentation and proper disposition.

According to PRO3, it was coordinating with the appropriate government agencies to determine the applicable violations to be filed against the arrested persons and to conduct further examination and verification of the recovered cigarette products. /gsg

MANILA, Philippines – A pair of blowout losses do not bode well for Gilas Pilipinas’ title defense prospects in the Asian Games, but head coach Tim Cone played down growing fears.

Instead, Cone shouldered the blame after the Philippines fell to South Korea by an average of 26.5 points in their two tune-up games, which formed part of both teams’ preparations for the quadrennial showpiece to be hosted in Nagoya, Japan.
The visiting Filipinos first absorbed an 81-55 defeat to the Koreans on Friday, September 4, then suffered a 69-42 rout on Sunday, September 6.

articles.title: PhilWeb’s multibillion bet on JKS gaming tech triggers PSE suspension
articles.summary: Fresh off Lance Gokongwei's P2-billion capital injection and appointment as chairman, PhilWeb is betting big on a multibillion-peso gaming tech investment that could define its turnaround

blocks.text: Fresh off Lance Gokongwei's P2-billion capital injection and appointment as chairman, PhilWeb is betting big on a multibillion-peso gaming tech investment that could define its turnaround

MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) will suspend trading in PhilWeb Corporation starting Tuesday, September 8, after the gaming technology firm disclosed a multibillion investment in JKS Tech Solutions Inc.

PhilWeb said on Monday, September 7, that it and wholly owned subsidiary PhilWeb Capital Corporation had signed subscription agreements covering a combined 10.73 million Common B shares of JKS at P394 apiece.
PhilWeb itself will subscribe to 3.41 million JKS shares worth about P1.34 billion, while PhilWeb Capital will take another 7.32 million shares.

The scale is what makes this investment significant. As of June 30, PhilWeb reported just P548.46 million in total assets against P741.95 million in liabilities. This left the company with negative stockholders’ equity of P193.48 million.
Those figures, however, came before the completion of JG Summit tycoon Lance Gokongwei’s P2-billion capital infusion into PhilWeb.

Even before the big boost of capital that Gokongwei provided, PhilWeb had already begun improving operationally, returning to profit in the first half with net income of P60.97 million, compared with a P41.77-million loss a year earlier.

The PSE said the JKS deal falls under its rules covering substantial acquisitions and reverse takeovers and will suspend PhilWeb shares beginning 9 am Tuesday while waiting for the company’s required comprehensive disclosure.

Under PSE rules, the substantial acquisition provision applies when a listed company or its subsidiary acquires a direct or indirect interest in an unlisted company equivalent to at least 10% of the listed firm’s total book value. PhilWeb’s P4.23-billion investment blows past that threshold: it is roughly 7.7 times the company’s entire P548.5-million asset base as of end-June, before the Gokongwei capital infusion was factored in.
Rappler has asked PhilWeb for its comment on the deal and suspension. This story will be updated once a response is received.
PhilWeb described JKS as a “Philippine B2B technology, platform and digital infrastructure company serving licensed mid-market operators in the digital entertainment sector.”

Beyond PhilWeb’s relatively dry description of JKS as a technology and digital infrastructure company, Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (PAGCOR) records reveal more about what the company actually does.

JKS is the PAGCOR-accredited gaming system administrator behind Epic Game, a regulated online gaming platform. Its approved offerings span traditional and electronic bingo, electronic casino games, sports betting, specialty games, and numeric games.

Money and shares are moving in both directions. In a separate disclosure on Monday, PhilWeb said JKS agreed to buy 81.38 million PhilWeb treasury shares for P16.50 each, paying a total of about P1.34 billion. The shares to be acquired represent around 4.85% of PhilWeb’s issued and outstanding shares, giving JKS a meaningful stake in the listed company once the transaction is completed.
The P1.34 billion that JKS will pay PhilWeb almost exactly matches PhilWeb’s own P1.34-billion direct subscription to JKS.
PhilWeb Capital Corporation, meanwhile, will subscribe to a much larger P2.88 billion worth of JKS shares. Monday’s disclosures did not specify how the PhilWeb subsidiary would fund that investment.

Nevertheless, PhilWeb has raised significant fresh capital in recent months, which could help fund its latest multibillion deal. In June, Gokongwei agreed to personally invest about P2.03 billion in the company through common and redeemable preferred shares priced at P8 apiece. PhilWeb said at the time that the money would strengthen its capital base and give it greater financial flexibility, including for “expansion opportunities and investments.”
Gokongwei acquired 159.53 million common shares on August 27 and was appointed PhilWeb chairman on the same day, replacing Crisanto Roy Alcid, who remained a director. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Threatening letters revive fears among Kashmiri Pandits
articles.summary: Leaked addresses and phone numbers have reignited fears among Hindu government employees who returned to Muslim-majority Kashmir under a rehabilitation scheme.

image.caption: Kashmiri Hindus, known locally as Pandits, have long complained of a lack of security [FILE: June 2022]Image: Channi Anand/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: A new wave of threatening letters targeting Kashmiri Pandits — members of the Hindu minority community who fled the Muslim-majority Kashmir Valley during a militant uprising in the 1990s — has deepened fears among those who have returned to the region as civil servants under an Indian government federal rehabilitation scheme.
The latest letters, which surfaced in the last week of August, named several employees. The letters also included their Jammu residential addresses, vehicle registration numbers and phone numbers.
Personal details exposed

"Similar threat letters surfaced in early August, but the latest contains our Jammu residential address, vehicle and phone numbers, which have also been shared on social media," Anil Koul, a government employee, told DW, urging authorities to investigate the source of the leak.

The letters have been attributed to a little-known group calling itself the United Liberation Council, which security officials suspect could be a front for the Pakistan-based Islamist militant outfit Lashkar-e-Taiba.

The group reportedly first surfaced in July, when it released a poster marking the death anniversary of a former militant commander. Authorities have yet to confirm the letters' authenticity or the existence of the group behind them.

The latest letters also distinguish between Pandits who never left the Valley — and are therefore "safe" — and those recruited under New Delhi's rehabilitation program, who are accused of working for "masters" outside Kashmir.
The fresh threats have also triggered a political row.

Jammu and Kashmir National Conference (JKNC) president and former Jammu and Kashmir chief minister, Farooq Abdullah, called them a "conspiracy" aimed at delaying the restoration of statehood, which the region lost in 2019.
Abdullah also questioned why Hindu officers from outside the region were not facing similar threats.
His remarks drew sharp criticism from Kashmiri Pandit groups and the ruling Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which accused him of being insensitive to the community's fears.
Familiar fears
Government records show 44,167 Kashmiri migrant families registered as having left since 1990 citing security concerns, of which 39,782 were Hindu.
For Pandit community representatives, however, the latest threats are part of a much longer security problem.

Sanjay Tickoo, president of the Kashmiri Pandit Struggle Committee (KPSS), said the threats should be viewed against the backdrop of targeted killings and repeated security concerns faced by Pandit government employees in the Valley. He blames security lapses and says repeated meetings with officials since a wave of killings in 2022 have failed to resolve their concerns.
"Since 2022, meetings have resulted in nothing," Tickoo told DW. He also wondered how those making the threats have access to employees' personal details.
"How are these details being posted on social media?" Tickoo asked.
Targeted killings have occurred sporadically in the years since. At least seven Kashmiri Pandits were killed by militants during a spike in violence between 2020 and 2022.
One of the starkest cases was that of Rahul Bhat, a Pandit revenue official who was shot dead inside his government office in Budgam in May 2022.
The last confirmed targeted killing of a Kashmiri Pandit was in October 2022, when Puran Krishan Bhat, an orchard farmer, was shot dead in Shopian district.
Former Jammu and Kashmir police chief S P Vaid described the latest threats as part of a familiar militant playbook.
"There is nothing new in this," Vaid told DW, calling it "a ploy by Pakistan to Islamize society." He said similar tactics had been used against migrant workers in the Valley.

The difference, this time, is the precision of the threats. Personal data that should not have been so easily accessible has been made public, and no clear explanation of how it was leaked has been provided.
Kashmir: Fears dampen celebrations at Hindu festival
The return dilemma

The KPSS estimates roughly 6,500 Pandits who never left the Valley, along with another 4,000 who have returned as government employees under a federal rehabilitation scheme, live in India-administered Kashmir.
But the reintegration of those who fled decades ago has proved challenging.
Rahul Pandita, a journalist and author of "Our Moon Has Blood Clots: A Memoir of a Lost Home in Kashmir," said the government's record on rehabilitation was inadequate.

"The BJP has had no rehabilitation policy for Kashmiri Hindus," Pandita told DW, arguing that the government employees in the Valley had returned under a policy introduced during the previous government of former Prime Minister Manmohan Singh.
Some land has been returned and cases of killings investigated, he said, but "it is too little and too late."
Pandita said the bigger problem was that no government could guarantee a completely secure environment for a mass return.

"No matter what the government does, the situation will never be conducive enough for the Pandits to return," he said, arguing that as long as Islamist militancy exists in the region, Kashmiri Hindus would still be targeted.
"It's for them then to decide if they are willing to take such a risk," he said.
Beyond government employees, some Pandits who have returned and established businesses in the Valley are already living there quietly, Pandita said.
"That is the best-case scenario for Kashmiri Pandits in Kashmir Valley," he said.

blocks.caption: Pandits accuse the government in New Delhi of not doing enough to protect them from alleged Islamist threatsImage: Firdous Nazir/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: Security beyond protection
Sushobha Barve, executive secretary of the Center for Dialogue and Reconciliation, said the latest threats expose a wider security paradox.
"Despite claims of normalcy, a tiny group of active militants has successfully disrupted the lives of migrant families. Breaking the cycle of panic is essential," Barve told DW.
She said there was also growing political frustration over the delay in restoring Jammu and Kashmir's statehood, arguing that this grievance cut across the region.

Amitabh Mattoo, an academic and professor of international relations at Jawaharlal Nehru University who has written extensively on Kashmir, said any return of Kashmiri Pandits had to be both secure and dignified.

"The state has an essential role in ensuring their physical security and in protecting their property, cultural and other legitimate rights. But security measures alone will not suffice," Mattoo told DW.
"A sustainable return will also require patient reconciliation, engagement with local civil society, and the gradual rebuilding of inter-community trust and social and economic ties."
How India reshaped Kashmir by revoking Article 370
