articles.title: Alex Eala full of gratitude despite painful US Open exit
articles.summary: Alex Eala says it is a “real privilege to experience” playing on tennis’ biggest stages and receiving overwhelming fan support even as her US Open run comes to a heartbreaking end

blocks.text: BELOVED. The Philippines' Alexandra Eala acknowledges the crowd after losing her third-round match against Iva Jovic of the United States in the 2026 US Open.
Robert Deutsch/IMAGN IMAGES/Reuters
Alex Eala says it is a “real privilege to experience” playing on tennis’ biggest stages and receiving overwhelming fan support even as her US Open run comes to a heartbreaking end

items: Alex Eala expressed gratitude despite her heartbreaking loss to Iva Jovic in the third round of the US Open, highlighting the support from the crowd at Arthur Ashe Stadium.
Eala showcased her determination by taking a set from Jovic and leading in the final set before ultimately losing, reflecting on her performance and the lessons learned.
Looking ahead, Eala is set to compete in the Singapore Open and the Asian Games, where she aims to contribute to the Philippine team's success.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – Even in the face of one of her most painful defeats, Alex Eala somehow still radiates gratitude.

Eala chooses to look at the silver lining after her US Open campaign came to a heartbreaking end following a stinging 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 loss to close friend Iva Jovic of the United States in the third round on Sunday, September 5 (Monday, September 6, Manila time).

The defeat denied Eala a chance to match her best Grand Slam showing — a fourth-round run in the Wimbledon Championships in July — but the Filipina world No. 18 relished her debut at the famed Arthur Ashe Stadium, buoyed by a passionate crowd rallying behind her.
“It’s indescribable to sum up the support and how it makes me feel in just a few words. It’s a real privilege to experience this in a lifetime,” said Eala, pausing to fight back tears.

“Playing on Arthur Ashe and feeling the support and being in those environments and learning these lessons and fighting and doing what I love, I’m really happy. I’m really lucky to have these opportunities, to have these people support me, and to be working hard, to be able to work hard, and to be able to live this life how I am living it.”
Eala proved she deserved to play at the world’s largest tennis stadium as she engaged world No. 14 Jovic in a three-hour thriller that kept those in attendance on the edge of their seats.

Swept by Jovic in both of their two previous encounters, Eala finally took a set from the American and even built a 4-2 lead in the decider before she ran out of gas, losing four of the last five games.
Although a breakthrough win against Jovic slipped through her fingers, Eala has every reason to hold her head high after battling until the final point.
“What I’ve learned tonight, I have yet to process. But I think that what I know for sure is that I left everything out there,” Eala said.

“I fought through the ups and downs. There were moments where I wasn’t playing so good, and moments where I was playing really good. So, what I know for a fact is that I fought. So, I’m happy with that.”
Eala gets a two-week break before she returns to action at the Singapore Open, which will run from September 21 to 27.

Then, from Singapore, the 21-year-old will fly to Japan for the Asian Games, where she is billed as one of the Philippines’ top gold-medal prospects following her bronze finish in the 2023 edition in China.
“I love playing and competing with the Philippine team,” said Eala. “I think it’s a really fun environment, and I love being with the team.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: Kenya minister warns foreigners against 'misusing' visas to trade
articles.summary: Kenya is due to start enforcing measures to restrict foreign nationals from operating small-scale businesses.

blocks.text: Kenya's trade ministry has warned foreign nationals that visa-free entry into the country does not grant them the right to work, as the government vows to shut down unlicensed small businesses run by foreigners.
President William Ruto had set today as the deadline for foreigners operating small-scale businesses to cease work.
Ahead of the move, the Burundian embassy in Kenya said it would offer emergency free travel documents to its citizens willing to go back home, amid reports of the mistreatment of Burundians.
It is unclear how many foreign nationals are involved in small-scale trading or how many would be affected by the crackdown.

In a statement, the trade ministry said there was a "deliberate misuse of visa applications by some visitors", adding that some entered Kenya as investors or tourists but then got involved in business activities in breach of their declared status.

"Owing to the high number of foreigners involved in the retail and local trade sectors, there is therefore a need to align their activities and ensure compliance with work permit provisions," Trade Minister Lee Kinyanjui said.
Last week, Ruto said that Kenya remained open to foreign investment, but it could not be "that a person comes from China or elsewhere to be a hawker or open a small shop".
He argued that investors should create jobs and expand production rather than compete with Kenyans in small businesses.
Ruto's comments sparked mixed reactions, with some critics describing them as a populist move that risked stoking xenophobia. Government officials deny the allegation.
Burundi's Foreign Affairs Minister Edouard Bizimana said in a post on X that "Kenyans in Burundi were living peacefully but if the hate speech against Burundi continues things will certainty change".
"Kenya government is responsible for the lives of Burundians living in Kenya," he added.
Bizimana's post followed an urgent meeting he held with representatives of the East African Community (EAC), an eight-member bloc which promotes economic integration in the region.
Both Kenya and Burundi are part of the group. Kenyan representatives attended the meeting called by Bizimana in Burundi.
Bizimana said he had asked the Kenyan ambassador to convey to his government Burundi's concerns and to ensure that no Burundian was subjected to abuse.
On Sunday, a top official in Kenya's foreign affairs ministry said foreigners, with the required documentation, including "work permits and licences", could continue their activities.

"Burundian nationals and all East Africans - and Africans for that matter - are free to live in Kenya as long as they conduct their businesses or work according to the requirements of our laws, Permanent Secretary Korir Sing'oei said.
The government's clarification, however, did little to ease concerns among some foreign traders.
Alexis Ntinanirwa, the head of the Association of Burundians living in Kenya, told the BBC Great Lakes service that he was unhappy with Ruto's decision, but was urging Burundians to remain patient.
He warned that the issue could have wider regional consequences because Kenyans are also involved in small-scale businesses in other East African countries.

"This issue is not only going to cause problems for Burundians working in Kenya, but it is also going to cause problems in the region because there are also Kenyans doing these small jobs in our countries in Burundi, Tanzania and Uganda."
Ntinanirwa advised Burundians involved in hawking and other small businesses to avoid confrontation with police.
Additional reporting by Akisa Wandera and Prime Ndikumagenge

articles.title: DICT mulls fewer valid IDs for SIM registration
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) is eyeing a reduction in the number of valid IDs accepted for SIM (subscriber identity module) registration to…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) is eyeing a reduction in the number of valid IDs accepted for SIM (subscriber identity module) registration to prevent identity falsification, Secretary Henry Aguda said on Monday.

During the House of Representatives committee on appropriations’ briefing on the DICT’s proposed 2027 budget, Aguda pointed out that the number of valid IDs accepted has become a problem in the SIM registration process.
“We in the NTC (National Telecommunications Commission) are thinking of reducing the types of IDs. They may be reduced to three: national ID, passport, and license,” he said.
Around 17 government-issued IDs can be used for SIM card registration, including the national ID, passport, driver’s license, and police and National Bureau of Investigation clearances, among others.
Aguda said using the national ID in the SIM registration process could make identity falsification impossible.
“So that’s what we are planning to do. Limit it to an ID that has a higher chance of having the correct identity and information,” he added.

Kabataan party-list Rep. Renee Co then expressed her support for advocacy groups raising privacy concerns about the SIM card registration process. She said the data used in the procedure must not be stored anywhere other than by the government.
“We’d like to discuss this to ensure that’s what will happen. Hash out policies so they won’t intrude on the right to privacy,” she added.

Last week, the Philippine National Police–Anti Cybercrime Group (PNP-ACG) raised concerns that almost all recent cybercrime cases in the country still involve SIM cards, as it called for amendments to the SIM Card Registration Act.

With this, the PNP-ACG proposed that SIM cards be authenticated and activated only after successful authentication and registration. The unit also expressed its preference to use only the national ID and suggested limiting SIM card ownership to a maximum of five per person. /mcm

articles.title: Cebu mourns death of National Artist Resil Mojares
articles.summary: CEBU CITY— The Philippine flag at the Cebu Provincial Capitol was flown at half-mast on Monday, Sept. 7, as Cebu mourned the death of National Artist for Literature Dr. Resil Mojares. Gov. Pamela…

blocks.text: CEBU CITY— The Philippine flag at the Cebu Provincial Capitol was flown at half-mast on Monday, Sept. 7, as Cebu mourned the death of National Artist for Literature Dr. Resil Mojares.

Gov. Pamela Baricuatro issued Executive Order (EO) No. 49 on Monday, directing Capitol employees to fly the Philippine flag at half-mast in honor of the renowned writer, historian, scholar and educator.
In the EO, Baricuatro described Mojares as a distinguished scholar whose life and work “brought pride and honor to Cebu” and made lasting contributions to Philippine literature, history and culture.

“The late Resil B. Mojares, National Artist for Literature, distinguished writer, historian, scholar, and educator, passed away on 5 September 2026 at the age of 83, leaving his family, friends, colleagues, students and the people of Cebu in deep sorrow,” Baricuatro said.
Tributes for the eminent Cebuano scholar poured in from colleagues, students, institutions and fellow historians across the country.
Historian Ambeth Ocampo said Cebu would be forever changed by Mojares’ passing, praising him for showing that a scholar could be deeply learned while remaining humble and warm.

“Cebu will not be the same without Resil Mojares, National Artist for Literature who showed, by example, how to wear erudition lightly, and how to be both an excellent scholar and wonderful person,” Ocampo said.

Archaeologist, fellow historian and longtime collaborator Jose Eleazer “Jobers” Bersales also paid tribute to Mojares, whose writing style he described as uniquely “Mojares-que” and difficult to replicate.

“Thank you most profoundly for the rare privilege, National Artist Dr. Resil Mojares. With your sudden passing, Cebu and the nation have lost their most precious literary gem,” Bersales said in a social media post.
The University of San Carlos (USC), where Mojares spent decades as a professor and which he considered his home, also mourned his passing.

“His work not only shaped the landscape of Philippine letters, but also deeply touched generations of students, educators, and scholars who had the privilege of learning from his wisdom,” USC said in a statement on social media.
Mojares was named a National Artist for Literature in 2018, cementing a career spanning literature, history, research, and education.
His work documented Cebu’s history and culture while contributing significantly to the study of Philippine literature.
His daughter, Leigh Go-Mojares, announced on social media that his wake will be held at Cebu Rolling Hills Memorial Chapels in Mandaue City.
“Thank you all for your kind messages and sharing your stories after the loss of our father, Resil. We appreciate all your thoughts and prayers,” Go-Mojares said.

articles.title: Russia opens first road bridge with North Korea
articles.summary: Russia and North Korea have opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River as political, economic and military ties between the two countries deepen.

image.caption: The new Russia-North Korea road bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's lifeImage: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Russia and North Korea on Monday cut the ribbon on the first road bridge linking the two countries as Moscow and Pyongyang deepen their strategic partnership.
The crossing spans the Tumen River and marks another expansion of transport links between the two countries.
Where is the new bridge?
The road crossing is near the existing Friendship Bridge, a railway bridge commissioned in 1959 following the Korean War.
Russia and North Korea already have direct rail and air connections, but until now there had been no road bridge between them.
The new bridge is named after Soviet Red Army officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korean founder Kim Il Sung's life. Relatives of Novichenko attended the opening ceremony.

blocks.caption: Nikolai Shcherbitsky and Tatyana Shcherbitskaya joined the ceremony to unveil the bridge named after their grandfather and father respectivelyImage: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance

blocks.text: Construction began in April 2025 after the project was agreed during Russian President Vladimir Putin's visit to North Korea in 2024.
Why is the road bridge being opened now?
Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said the new crossing should boost economic development, tourism and employment.

"I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation," the TASS news agency quoted Mishustin as saying by video link at the opening ceremony.
Relations between Moscow and Pyongyang have strengthened considerably since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
North Korea sent thousands of troops to Russia's Kursk region to help Russian forces repel a Ukrainian incursion launched in 2024.

articles.title: Germany's far-right AfD says 'democracy demands' parties work with them after state election win
articles.summary: The far-right party is trying to form a government in the state after falling three seats short of a majority.

blocks.text: The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is "very, very close" to taking power, its deputy parliamentary leader has told the BBC, after a historic victory in elections for the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.
Sunday's preliminary results show it fell three seats short of an outright majority, with 43.8% of the vote. It is now seeking support from other parties or individuals in order to govern.
While most German political parties refuse to work with the AfD, Beatrix von Storch called for its opponents to enter talks and said: "You cannot say I do not accept the vote of the people".
No far-right party has controlled a German state since World War Two, and governing at state level would mean powers over policing and local education.
Von Storch said if parties refused to work with the AfD, "then we might end up in severe chaos and maybe we have a new election".
Her comments were echoed by AfD's leader in Saxony-Anhalt, Ulrich Siegmund, who told a news conference on Monday that the party had won a "clear mandate to govern".
Saxony-Anhalt has a small population of 2.1 million and the AfD in the state is assessed by domestic intelligence as "right-wing extremist", a classification rejected by Siegmund, 35.
Siegmund said discussions with other parties were initiated on Sunday night and could potentially take days or weeks to conclude.
"We reach out to everybody first, we will have consultations and then we'll see whether [there are] individual parliamentary groups or MPs who would be willing to help us," he added.
The AfD is currently heading for 39 seats in the 83-seat state parliament instead of the 42 needed for an outright majority, although the result has not yet been finalised.

Von Storch told the BBC the AfD was talking to individuals within the conservative CDU group - the largest party in both the state's outgoing coalition and Germany's government - because they were "very, very unhappy with their own party".
In Saxony-Anhalt, the CDU won 17.2% of the vote, according to preliminary results.
One idea being floated is whether there could be informal deal whereby a small party - the BSW - could give their tacit support to allow the AfD to form a minority government.
The left-wing populist BSW, which is set to win five seats, is also tough on migration and backs importing Russian gas.
The AfD has signalled an openness to talk with other parties but all - apart from the BSW - refuse to co-operate with the far-right.
The AfD leads the opinion polls nationally, ahead of the ruling conservatives of Chancellor Friedrich Merz and the Social Democrats, but their heartland lies in the eastern states.
They also won the 2024 state election in neighbouring Thuringia, but failed to secure enough seats to win power.

Among the AfD's policies is a highly controversial plan for "remigration", which is widely understood to mean mass deportations of migrants, although the party says it refers to deporting criminals and those in the country illegally.

articles.title: Russia and North Korea open first road bridge across their shared border
articles.summary:
Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine

Russia and North Korea have opened

blocks.text: Russia and North Korea have opened the first road bridge across their shared border, in the latest sign of the rapidly deepening ties between the two countries since the start of the war in Ukraine.

The one-kilometre bridge spans the Tumen River between Khasan in Russia’s far east and Tumangang in North Korea, along a remote and sparsely populated stretch of the countries’ shared border just a few miles from the coast.

Speaking by video link during the bridge’s opening ceremony on Monday, Russia’s prime minister, Mikhail Mishustin, said the new crossing would spur development in a range of areas, including tourism, while creating new jobs

“I am convinced that the expansion of cross-border transport infrastructure will provide a powerful impetus for the further development of trade, economic, scientific, technological and cultural cooperation,” Mishustin said.
The road bridge is named after the Soviet officer Yakov Novichenko, who is credited with saving North Korea’s founding leader, Kim Il-sung, from an assassination attempt by a pro-South Korean group.
After the opening ceremony, convoys of vehicles crossed the bridge from both sides.
Russia and the secretive North Korea regime are already connected by a railway bridge across the Tumen, as well as regular flights between Vladivostok and Pyongyang.
Ukrainian human rights groups have warned that the bridge may be intended to provide a discreet military logistics corridor between the two countries.

Truth Hounds, a Ukrainian human rights organisation, has described it as a likely future corridor for moving North Korean troops, construction brigades and military officials into Russia, while allowing Russian technology and resources to travel in the opposite direction with less risk of detection.

Ties between Moscow and Pyongyang have strengthened dramatically since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. North Korea has sent thousands of troops to Russia’s Kursk region to help Moscow repel a Ukrainian incursion launched there in 2024.
In return, Russia is believed to have provided North Korea with air-defence missiles, electronic warfare equipment, drones and spy-satellite technology, according to South Korean intelligence.

Russian and North Korean officials have also touted North Korea as a new holiday destination since the country reopened to Russian tourists in 2024, with thousands of Russians visiting its newly opened beach resorts and ski slopes since then.
Russia’s increasingly close embrace of totalitarian North Korea has raised eyebrows even in Moscow.

During an interview with the Russian broadcaster RBC last month, a reporter asked Sergei Lavrov, Russia’s longtime foreign minister, how the country had “ended up” with just “two allies – North Korea and Iran”.
Lavrov pushed back against the premise, saying there was “nothing wrong” with such company.
At the same time, some of Russia’s traditional partners have shown growing frustration with Moscow’s continuing war in Ukraine and the fallout it has caused across the region.

During a meeting in July, Kazakhstan’s president, Kassym-Jomart Tokayev, a longtime ally of Moscow, told the Russian president, Vladimir Putin, that he was hearing from leaders of many countries who questioned why Russia was still waging the war.
“The nature of the conflict isn’t entirely clear for many, including us,” Tokayev told Putin.

articles.title: Radiohead announce 2027 tour with shows in Australia and Japan
articles.summary:
UK band will play 16 shows across Perth, Melbourne and Sydney, as well as five shows in Saitama

Radiohead will return to Australia to play 16 shows across three cities next year, marking the…

blocks.text: Radiohead will return to Australia to play 16 shows across three cities next year, marking the band’s first tour of the country in 15 years.
On Monday afternoon, the British rock band unveiled the itinerary for its May 2027 tour, which also includes five shows in Japan.
The series of shows will kick off at Perth’s RAC Arena on 3 May for four performances in the city. This will be followed by six shows at Melbourne’s Rod Laver Arena and Sydney’s Afterpay Arena.

The band last toured Australia after their 2011 album the King of Limbs, although frontman Thom Yorke visited Australia for solo shows in 2024. During a Melbourne performance, Yorke walked off stage after being heckled by a pro-Palestine protester in the crowd. He returned a few minutes later to perform his final song of the evening, Radiohead’s 1997 hit Karma Police.
Last year, Radiohead reunited after seven years for a string of shows in European cities.
The band will also return to Japan for the first time in 19 years with five concerts at the GMO Arena Saitama near Tokyo.
The band has not recorded a studio album since 2016’s A Moon Shaped Pool. But the absence of new material has not quelled demand, with a frenzied rush for tickets when the shows were announced.
Radiohead first toured Australia in 1994 after the band’s debut album Pablo Honey, which contained their breakthrough hit Creep.

Fans can register interest for tickets to the Australian shows on an online portal – run by co-promoter Frontier Touring – that opened on Monday evening. It will create a ballot-like process to “help give fans fair access to tickets and minimise automated and unauthorised purchases.”
Tickets are capped at four for each city the band is performing in, the portal said.
“There’s no benefit to registering earlier. Every completed registration received by the deadline will be treated equally,” the website said.
Registration closes on Thursday at 5pm AEST. Successful registrants will be emailed with next steps from Friday and given a chance to buy tickets next week.

James Patrick Cruz/Rappler
(1st UPDATE) The former House speaker may be detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas – the designated detention center for flood control-related cases

items: The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division issued a warrant of arrest for Leyte 1st District Representative Martin Romualdez over a P7.44-billion plunder case.
Romualdez is accused of receiving kickbacks from co-accused Zaldy Co and using the funds to establish shell companies, with evidence provided by multiple witnesses.
As plunder is non-bailable, Romualdez will be detained upon arrest, with the court confirming the issuance of the warrant and a hold departure order.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – The Sandiganbayan 3rd Division issued a warrant of arrest on Monday, September 7 against Leyte 1st District Representative and former House speaker Martin Romualdez over his P7.44-billion plunder case.

Plunder is non-bailable, so Romualdez will likely be held under police custody once he is arrested by the Philippine National Police or surrenders to authorities. He is also likely to be detained at the New Quezon City Jail in Payatas – the designated detention center for flood control-related cases.

blocks.caption: Martin Romualdez charged with plunder

blocks.text: The Office of the Ombudsman filed the plunder case earlier on Monday against Romualdez and his co-accused: former Ako Bicol representative Zaldy Co, Joselyn Serenio, and Felicito Guevarra. Co is at large.
Romualdez allegedly received P7.44 billion in kickbacks from Co.

“Based on our investigation, Romualdez allegedly received kickbacks around 15 times from Co’s staff, from September 2022 to 2025. That’s for the P2-billion monthly quota or collections Romualdez imposed on Co,” the Ombudsman said in Filipino.

“Serenio received the cash delivery in the lawmaker’s different houses and properties. Romualdez used nearly P5 billion from these kickbacks to establish shell or dummy companies like Golden Pheasant Holdings Corporation, Braavos Holdings Opc, and Valiant Consolidated Resources, Inc.,” it added.

According to the Ombudsman, their case against Romualdez and co-accused stands on the evidence and testimonies from several witnesses, including former Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) undersecretary Roberto Bernardo and former DPWH Bulacan district engineer Henry Alcantara, among others.
At past 5 pm on Monday, the Sandiganbayan 3rd Division confirmed that it had issued a warrant and hold a departure order against Romualdez and fellow accused.

“The issuance of a warrant of arrest signifies only that, after personally evaluating the records, the Court found probable cause to believe that the accused committed the offense charged. Probable cause for the issuance of a warrant of arrest exists when the facts and circumstances alleged by the prosecution would lead a reasonably discreet and prudent person to believe that an offense has been committed by the person sought to be arrested,” said the 3rd Division.
Department of the Interior and Local Government chief Juanito Victor “Jonvic” Remulla also confirmed that Romualdez’s warrant had been signed Monday afternoon.
“Yes. We have confirmed that it has already been signed,” Remulla told Rappler. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Nepal observes national day of mourning for victims of flash flood disaster
articles.summary: Flags flew at half mast on the 13th day since the disaster, the last day of the Hindu mourning period.

blocks.text: Nepalis observed a national day of mourning for the victims of the flash flood on Monday, lighting candles to mark the last day of the traditional 13-day Hindu mourning period.
While flags were flown at half mast, commemorations were scaled back as rescue teams continue to search for survivors. Candlelight vigils were planned for Monday evening.

At least 1,287 people are known to have died after a flash flood, believed to have been triggered by a glacial collapse, swept through villages in a Himalayan valley along border between Nepal and Tibet.
Almost two weeks later, more than 5,000 people are still missing.

Phanindra Paudel of the National Emergency Operation Centre (NEOC) told the Reuters news agency that there would be "no government programmes organised as the rescue and search operation is still going on in the flood-hit areas."
Nepal's president, Ram Chandra Paudel, toured areas devastated by the floods on Monday, an aide told Reuters.
The home ministry said that government offices, as well as missions abroad, would fly the national flag at half mast to mark the final day of the mourning period.

Australian tunnel rescue expert Arnold Dix, who is advising Nepali teams, said in an update on X that the operation meant facing "multiple potential rescues, unfolding at the same time, in different places, each with its own dangers, uncertainties and lives that may still be saved."
Four people have been rescued in recent days, three at hydropower stations or tunnels.
On Saturday, a 64-year-old Nepali woman was pulled from her buried house on Saturday, more than 10 days after a wall of ice, rock and mud partially buried her house in the Nuwakot district.
She was discovered alive on the fourth floor of the building by Nepal's Armed Police Force and airlifted to a hospital in Kathmandu for treatment.
On Sunday rescue workers in China recovered twelve bodies in the Nepal-Tibet border, using excavators, shovels and ground penetrating radar at the site.

articles.title: Australia’s top bureaucrats want to block sharing of clips from parliament on social media to save them from ‘ridicule’
articles.summary:
Secretaries board concerned material posted without proper context as Greens warn ban could result in lack of transparency

  • Get our
articles.byline: Sarah Basford Canales and Tom McIlroy

blocks.text: The nation’s top bureaucrats want the Albanese government to ban video footage from parliamentary hearings being edited and shared on social media, in an extraordinary attempt to stop online ridicule and abuse.

But the Greens say highly paid public service chiefs shouldn’t be allowed to control footage from open parliamentary hearings, warning the proposed controls would limit a key tool of government transparency.

The secretaries board – made up of the heads of government departments and chaired by the Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet boss, Steven Kennedy – said they were concerned about material from hearings being presented online without proper context.
Politicians and political parties doing so exposed officials to “ridicule, hostility and abuse”, the board said.

“Recognising the evidence provided to a committee is on the public record, these officials have not consented to a subsequent use of their image, or its use by parliamentarians and their political parties for party-political purposes,” the board said in a submission published on Monday.
“In our view, the use of officials’ likenesses and their evidence in this way has the potential to be harmful both to the individual and the public sector as a whole.”

If the recommendations are not taken up, the board called for rules that would stop videos being edited or having captions added. Politicians would also be stopped from sharing content or commentary that targets individual officials for ridicule or harassment.

Calling for footage of full hearings and transcripts to be made available instead of clips, and for comments to be disabled, the board said its proposal would ensure “that scrutiny remains focused on evidence, administration and accountability rather than becoming personal”.

The proposal also includes concerns that members of parliament might not have a clear understanding of the role and responsibilities of public servants, when compared with government ministers. The board called for clearer explanation, including for newer MPs.

The push comes after the defence department deputy secretary Celia Perkins told a parliamentary hearing last week that public servants giving evidence did not consent to footage being shared on social media.

“They do not consent to the reposting of our evidence to social media sites or the reproduction of our likenesses for the purposes outside the framework of the parliament and the transparent public proceedings of this committee,” Perkins said.
The Senate foreign affairs, defence and trade committee rejected Perkins’ request on the advice of the Senate clerk.
Greens senator Steph Hodgins-May told Guardian Australia that members of the public had the right to see footage from hearings into government scrutiny.
“Bureaucrats shouldn’t get to decide where to draw the line on parliamentary scrutiny, particularly when they’re the ones being scrutinised,” she said.
“Of course debate should be respectful, but restricting what parliamentarians can post from public proceedings is not the answer.

“This looks like an attempt to take the teeth out of parliamentary scrutiny. Australians deserve more transparency and accountability, not less. And frankly, if this scrutiny wasn’t having an impact, they wouldn’t be so worried about it.”
The secretaries board includes all departmental chiefs, the Australian Public Service commissioner and the chief executive of the National Indigenous Australians Agency.

image.caption: Rescue workers search for victims under the rubble of a building destroyed in an Israeli airstrike in the southern village of Kfar Rumman, Lebanon, on Monday. (Mohammed Zaatari/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World
Israeli strikes on a southern Lebanese town early on Monday killed at least 11 people including two children and two medics, Lebanon's state news agency said.
2 children were killed in the airstrike on the town of Kfar Rumman, news report says

Israel has intensified its bombardment of south Lebanon in recent days despite a June ceasefire that was meant to halt fighting between the Israeli military and Lebanese armed group Hezbollah. At least seven people were killed in Israeli strikes on Sunday.
Just after midnight, Israeli warplanes hit a residential building in the town of Kfar Rumman in southern Lebanon, killing nine people including two children, Lebanon's National News Agency reported.
A separate Israeli drone strike on a civilian vehicle in the town killed two medics inside the car, it said.

According to The Associated Press, Lebanon's Health Ministry said one of the strikes hit a building, killing eight people — including a child and two women. It added that 11 people were also wounded, including four children and two women.
No evacuation warning

The strikes on the town came without an online evacuation warning from the Israeli military. The Israeli military did not immediately respond to Reuters' questions on the strikes, including whether it was aware of the presence of medics and children at the strike locations and why no evacuation warning was issued.

A spokesperson for the Israeli military issued a separate evacuation warning just after 2:00 a.m. local time for areas around a building in another town in southern Lebanon where it said it would strike Hezbollah facilities.

items: Israeli strikes kill 4 in southern Lebanon

blocks.text: Israeli strikes on Lebanon have killed more than 4,300 people since Hezbollah launched rockets at Israel on March 2 — two days after the start of U.S. and Israeli strikes on Iran — triggering an Israeli air and ground offensive.
The ceasefire saw violence decrease dramatically, but Israeli troops occupying swathes of southern Lebanon have continued razing villages in the self-declared security zone.
Israel's military has continued carrying out strikes both within the zone and to its north, mostly without evacuation warnings.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that a Russian drone which struck the headquarters of Ukraine's SBU security service in Kyiv on Friday had been aimed directly at the office of the agency's chief.
The revelation adds to the significance of one of the most high-profile Russian strikes on a Ukrainian government building since the start of the full-scale invasion.
SBU chief Oleksandr Poklad was not there at the time and was unharmed.

The strike also damaged nearby buildings and shattered windows in the area.
It was the first time the SBU headquarters had been hit since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in 2022.

The SBU plays a central role in Ukraine's war effort and has carried out long-range and covert operations against Russian military targets. It was behind Operation Spiderweb in 2025, when drones targeted Russian strategic bombers at air bases deep inside Russia, as well as the 2022 bombing of the bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea.

articles.title: The story of Canada’s 'only union-built town'
articles.summary: Founded on Newfoundland's Bonavista Peninsula more than a century ago, Port Union is called Canada’s only union-built town. It was the brainchild of union organizer William F. Coaker, who wanted to…

image.caption: Port Union on Newfoundland and Labrador’s Bonavista Peninsula was founded by the Fishermen’s Protective Union in 1916. (Submitted by Ainsley Hawthorn)

blocks.text: Nfld. & Labrador

Founded on Newfoundland's Bonavista Peninsula more than a century ago, Port Union is called Canada’s only union-built town. It was the brainchild of union organizer William F. Coaker, who wanted to help fishers get better working and living conditions.
N.L.’s Port Union was created to end the exploitation of fishermen by the merchant class
You might have heard of “union towns” — blue-collar cities like Chicago, Ill., and Scranton, Pa., where labour unions exercised enormous political power.
But perhaps nowhere has a better claim to be a “union town” than a small community on Newfoundland and Labrador’s Bonavista Peninsula.
Port Union wasn’t just run by unions, it was founded by one. Parks Canada and the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador call it Canada’s only union-built town.
The community was the brainchild of union organizer William F. Coaker.

The fifth of seven children, Coaker was forced to leave school at age 11 to help support his family. As a fish handler on the St. John’s harbourfront, he had a firsthand view of exploitative labour practices and instigated his first strike when he was just 13-years-old.
After learning the merchants he was working for were paying their young employees less than rival firms, he convinced all the boys to stop work until they received a raise.

Coaker represented their grievance to management, and they blockaded the entrances to the merchants’ premises to keep out scabs. Under pressure to offload the ships arriving in the harbour at the end of the fishing season, the company conceded two days later and raised the boys’ pay by a third.
Over the following years, Coaker travelled around the island and took on a variety of jobs, from store manager to telegraph operator to farmer.
His interest in labour rights only grew as he saw the way rural fishing families were mistreated by the merchant class.

Working under the “truck system,” they lived in a near-constant state of debt. Merchants ran the local stores where families bought clothing, dry goods, fishing supplies and other essentials on credit in the winter and spring. In the fall, they paid back what they owed with their catch of salt cod.

The problem was, the merchants not only set the local price of cod, concealing its true value on the international market, they also rarely disclosed the price of the goods families were buying upfront. When they settled accounts in the fall, the merchants could manipulate the prices to keep the fishers in debt and keep the firms from having to pay out any cash.
Coaker’s solution was unionization. Through collective action, fishers could fight for fair treatment.
In 1908, he founded the Fishermen’s Protective Union (FPU). Its goal was to improve quality of life for outport Newfoundlanders through education, policy and self-representation.

The union published a newspaper, the Fisherman’s Advocate, which printed weekly reports of foreign fish prices to help fishermen negotiate fair pay. It established its own trading company to import fishing gear at cost and export members’ cod directly to international markets, paying them in cash instead of credit.

The FPU advocated for a minimum wage, free public schools, and old age pensions. In 1913, its political arm — the Union Party — successfully elected eight members to the House of Assembly, including Coaker.
Seeking a headquarters for the union and unable to find something suitable in St. John’s, in 1915 Coaker bought an unoccupied 80-acre stretch of coastline on the southern shore of Trinity Bay.

The site had several features to recommend it. It was in a prime inshore fishing area where many FPU members lived, its harbour was ice-free from April to February with room enough to shelter a hundred boats, there was a nearby river ripe for hydro-electric development, and, most importantly, it could be acquired for just $400.

Construction crews broke ground in May 1916. Along the curve of the shoreline they built the commercial properties: a salt fish plant and general store, the factory building with its woodworking shop and printing press for the Fishermen’s Advocate, a forge and a shipyard.
Rising up the hillside that flanks the harbour, they installed rows of neat red duplexes to house the staff and managers of the FPU companies.
Union members moved in from outports along the northeast coast, and, by 1926, Port Union was a thriving community with its own hotel, bakery, post office, church, and railway station.

The union’s ethos wasn’t to provide the bare minimum to keep body and soul together. They believed working-class rural fish harvesters were as deserving of comforts and conveniences as wealthy urban merchants.

The town had its own soft drink plant and movie theatre, amenities unheard of in most outports at the time, and the factory boasted an elevator, possibly the only one outside of St. John’s. The houses had indoor plumbing, municipal sewer services and electricity provided by the town’s new hydro-electric plant on the Catalina River.
The town remained relatively prosperous until the cod moratorium of 1992, when the local fish plant was closed and a third of the population left.
Because of its unique history, Port Union has been designated a National Historic District, and some of its buildings have been converted to historic sites, museums and a community art space.
The Fishermen’s Protective Union may have been swept away by the tides of time, but its legacy lives on.

The union movement broke the cycle of debt that once kept fishing families in grinding poverty. The social policies FPU promoted, like free public education and minimum wages, have become fundamental to our democracy.
As for Port Union, it embodied a dream many are still fighting for to this day: a world where all people reap the benefits of their own hard work.

articles.title: Weather tracker: Typhoon Saudel causes mass evacuations in south-east China
articles.summary:
Torrential rain causes widespread damage; while north-west South Africa hit by thunderstorms and central-southern US faces oppressive heat

Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to…

blocks.text: Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to the Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China last week. The city of Putian, in Fujian province, recorded 416.5mm of rain in a 24-hour period between Thursday and Friday, with surrounding villages recording more than 500mm in the same period. In Fujian, authorities estimate that almost 600,000 people were evacuated from high-risk, flood-prone areas. A further 128,000 people in 53 counties were also affected across Jiangxi, with emergency evacuations affecting 9,000 people.

Flooding, landslips and infrastructure damage were reported widely in the region. More than 2,500 teachers and students were trapped in a school compound in the Zhejiang city of Wenzhou on Wednesday after extreme rainfall caused flash floods in low-lying areas. At least 1,260 people reportedly had to be rescued in Putian after a river embankment collapsed on Thursday, flattening 100 homes. On Saturday, a landslip in a village of Suichuan county, in Jiangxi province, killed three people and nine others remaining missing.
This is the seventh typhoon to affect China this year, and Saudel arrived shortly after Typhoon Narra dumped heavy rain on Guangdong, Hainan and Guangxi late last month.

The South African Weather Service implemented several thunderstorm warnings late last week, covering a large swathe of the northern and western provinces. Disruptive rainfall, damaging winds, excessive lightning and hail were all reported, with rainfall totals expected to have reached at least 75-100mm for parts of the Northern Cape and North West provinces over the weekend. In Johannesburg, eight families were evacuated from an apartment building after strong winds tore off a significant part of its roof.

Oppressive heat in the US affected states across the central-southern plains and the Mississippi valley this weekend, with maximum temperatures easily reaching the high 30s (Celsius; high 90s Fahrenheit). However, with high humidities, the heat indices in this region have been closer to 40-43C (105–110F). The unrelenting temperatures will continue across the midwest and southern US this week, with maximum temperatures continuing to reach the high 30s.

articles.title: DICT hopes Roblox-national ID age verification integration can be template for Meta
articles.summary: The DICT hopes success with integrating Roblox's age verification mechanisms with the national ID system can serve as a technical and policy template that Meta can follow

blocks.text: DICT. Department of Information and Communications Technology Secretary Henry Aguda on September 7, 2026.
Screenshot from House of Representatives Livestream
The DICT hopes success with integrating Roblox's age verification mechanisms with the national ID system can serve as a technical and policy template that Meta can follow

items: DICT Secretary Henry Aguda expressed hope that integrating Roblox's age verification and the Philippines' national ID system can serve as a model for Meta's social media age verification.
During a budget hearing, Aguda discussed a meeting with Meta and Roblox, where Roblox proposed using the national ID for age verification, allowing API calls based on digital biometrics.

Meta acknowledged technical challenges in implementing such integration globally and is sending a team to assess feasibility, while also making changes in the US following a settlement regarding teen access to its platforms.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) Secretary Henry Aguda said the agency hopes success with integrating Roblox’s age verification mechanisms with the national ID system can serve as a technical and policy template that Meta can follow when it comes to social media age verification.
During the House committee on appropriations’ DICT budget hearing on Monday, September 7, Aguda was asked about the outcome of the meeting with Meta in Singapore as it related to age verification.

He explained that during the meeting — with social media company Meta Platforms and game development platform company Roblox — Roblox themselves broached the topic of using an integration of the Philippines’ national ID with their age verification systems.

According to Aguda, such a proposed system would simply be a qualifier to determine if a user is a certain age that can use specific age tiers of Roblox accounts. He said there is an eVerify solution within the national ID system that may allow for such to happen.

“Kahit na wala pang physical card, basta yung digital biometrics niyo nandoon na sa Philippine Statistics Authority, puwede na sila mag API calls.” (Even wihout a physical card, as long as the digital biometrics are with the Philippine Statistics Authority, they can make API calls.) These API or Application Programming Interface calls would allow Roblox to tell if a user is getting the content appropriate for their account.

blocks.caption: LIST: What Roblox has done to safeguard child users

blocks.text: According to Aguda, Meta cited technical complexities in performing this as it has not done such an integration anywhere in the world, and is worried that it would make around 170 countries it serves follow suit in requesting similar accommodations.
Meta is making some changes to how it operates in the United States in light of a settlement with US states that would add limits to how teens gain access and use its various social media platforms.
Aguda said Meta will send a technical working team to study the feasibility of the plans they’ve discussed with the DICT.

“We are hoping that if Roblox is successful in the integration, it can become a technical and policy template for the other social media platforms to follow,” Aguda said in a mix of English and Filipino.
The DICT is seeking P19.491 billion for its fiscal year 2027 budget. – Rappler.com

blocks.text: Britishminister Emma Reynolds on Monday slammed "thuggish" anti-migrant protests that blocked roads in the English coastal city of Portsmouth.
Hundreds of protesters gathered in Portsmouth on Sunday following the arrival of about 140 migrants who had crossed the English Channel from France, UK media reported.
"This is thuggish and intimidating behavior," Reynolds, who is Chief Secretary to the Treasury, told Sky News, adding that the police brought the Portsmouth protest under control.
The demonstration came a day after masked protesters disrupted traffic at Dover terminal, blocking routes to the busy ferry port.
Masked protesters in Dover
On Saturday, hundreds of masked people blocked traffic at England's port of Dover as part of an anti-migrant protest, halting ferry traffic between France and the UK.

Video footage showed demonstrators, reportedly backed by far-right groups, in balaclavas chanting "stop the boats," in a reference to refugees and migrants who attempt the dangerous English Channel crossing in a bid to reach Great Britain.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham's Labour Party government said that "the right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but we condemn the behavior in Dover and the travel disruption it has caused."
The Dover demonstration caused a traffic jam of about four miles (6.4 km) and temporarily halted traffic into and out of the port.
Britain has struggled for years to curb small-boat crossings from France, although Reynolds said arrivals were down 43% from last year to about 17,000 so far this year.

articles.title: Minister condemns ‘thuggish’ far-right, anti-migrant protesters in Portsmouth – UK politics live
articles.summary:
Emma Reynolds says demonstrations ‘cross a line’

Good morning. John Healey is giving his first major speech on economic policy since he became chancellor seven weeks ago.…

blocks.text: Minister condemns ‘thuggish’ far-right, anti-migrant protesters in Portsmouth

Good morning. John Healey is giving his first major speech on economic policy since he became chancellor seven weeks ago. It is meant to be the main government news of the morning and, as Pippa Crerar writes in her preview story, Healey will argue the government’s plans to boost growth across the whole country will enable the British economy to “turn a corner”.
Healey’s deputy, Emma Reynolds, the chief secretary to the Treasury, has been giving interviews as part of the build-up.

But, as well as taking questions about growth and tax, Reynolds has also found herself taking questions about the latest far-right protest about immigration, triggered by a large boat carrying migrants arriving for the first time in Portsmouth.
Commenting on the behaviour of the protesters, who blocked roads and some of whom were masked, Reynolds said:

double quotation markThis is thuggish and intimidating behaviour. This is not peaceful protest. Obviously, as a politician, I absolutely support people’s right to peaceful protest. But this crosses a line and I just want to take the opportunity to thank the police and other emergency services who have brought this under control. We do not want to see this kind of behaviour anywhere, frankly.
Here is the agenda for the day.
Around 9.30am: John Healey, the chancellor, gives a speech on economic growth in the West Midlands.
11.30am: Downing Street holds a lobby briefing.
2.30pm: Angela Rayner, the housing secretary, takes questions in the Commons.
After 3.30pm: Emma Reynolds, the chief secretary to the Treasury, is due to make a statement to MPs.
Afternoon: MPs start debating the remaining stages of the health bill.
And Chris Bryant, the Northern Ireland secretary, is today meeting the Northern Ireland political leaders, as MLAs (members of the legislative assembly) return to Stormont after the summer recess.

blocks.text: Healey says he wants growth story 'written in more places'
John Healey is about to deliver his speech on the economy. Here are extracts that were released overnight by the Treasury.
On the UK turning the corner

double quotation markA new story about Britain. An optimistic story. One of resilience. Pride. Huge latent potential. A country turning a corner. A country whose people, businesses and communities are ready to seize the opportunity of new technologies and new ideas.
On what makes good growth

double quotation markAsk an economist what growth is and you’ll get a number. But ask the country and you’ll get a different answer. A young person getting a new job in a company that’s on the up. A sole trader winning a new contract that pays for a holiday with their kids. A business winning a new export order, giving the community around it a new lease of life.” The prime minister laid out a clear diagnosis of what has gone wrong in the past. The solution is a fundamental shift that starts with putting power in the right places. The next chapter of Britain’s growth story will be written in more places.
On the importance of wealth creation

double quotation markInstead of getting in the way with complexity and red tape, we need a strong, strategic centre wired to enable local leaders and their ambitions. That’s why we created No 10 North, working on a dual mission with the Treasury, removing obstacles so that local leaders and businesses can pull together to drive growth and productivity. I want to see wealth creation in this country. I want to see businesses make a profit. And to create the conditions for that we need an active, accountable state at all levels to remove blockages and create the conditions for more investment.
