articles.title: LPG crisis deepens in Kathmandu, restaurants on the brink
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — The cooking gas shortage has deepened in the Kathmandu Valley, with consumers saying they are being forced to return empty-handed despite queuing for hours for a cylinder. The…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — The cooking gas shortage has deepened in the Kathmandu Valley, with consumers saying they are being forced to return empty-handed despite queuing for hours for a cylinder.
The shortage has also pushed restaurants and small eateries to the brink of closure, as an already uncertain supply of liquefied petroleum gas has become increasingly difficult to manage.

The scarcity follows the closure of the Krishnabhir section of the Mugling-Naubise road along the Prithvi Highway, the main supply route to Kathmandu Valley. The disruption has severely affected the movement of essential goods into the capital.

Amid the shortage, LPG refilling plant operators have raised the price by Rs100 to Rs105 per cylinder, saying the cost of transporting cooking gas through alternative routes has increased.The official price of a refilled cylinder, in exchange for an empty one, is Rs2,060.
Consumer rights activists, however, have expressed concern over the price increase at a time when households are already struggling to secure cylinders.
On Saturday, Nagendra Sah, managing director of Nepal Oil Corporation, came under public criticism after he said that cooking gas was still cheaper than a kilogramme of mutton.

Consumer rights activists and restaurant operators said the remark was insensitive and argued that the state-owned supply utility should be focused on ensuring uninterrupted supplies rather than making comparisons with the price of other commodities.
Manisha Bhurtel, who works at a clothing store in the Pepsicola area, has been trying to obtain a cylinder for a month. She visits a nearby cooking gas depot almost every day.
“I am getting more anxious every day. I don’t even have an electric stove,” said Bhurtel, who lives with her family of three in a rented room.
“I have two children and a grandmother. I am worried about feeding my family,” she said.
Amrit Bhusal bought an electric stove a few months ago when it became increasingly difficult to get cooking gas.

“We were managing to prepare meals using an electric stove and LPG. Relying solely on an electric stove is not a solution as electricity is also not regular,” said Bhusal, who lives in a rented room in Imadol.
“I have two cylinders and both are empty. I have been searching for at least one cylinder for five days,” he said.

blocks.caption: Nepal Oil Corporation, in a press statement issued on Sunday, said that until the Prithvi Highway resumes, LPG cylinders would be supplied after being refilled at plants in Tarai districts and transported to Kathmandu through alternative routes.  Photo: Nepal Photo Library

blocks.text: With the Teej festival approaching and relatives expected to visit, Bhusal said he was worried about how his family would manage the preparations.
“It is difficult to know how we will manage the festive preparations,” he said.
The shortage is also hitting restaurants hard.

Restaurant owners said they are on the verge of shutting down their businesses because they could not count on a regular supply of cooking gas. Nepal Oil Corporation last week said it would prioritise the distribution of LPG cylinders to household consumers.

“The dealers have stopped supplying cooking gas. The government has told us to arrange it ourselves, but that is not easy. The transportation costs are too high,” said an official at Bagaicha Restaurant, which operates multiple outlets in the Kathmandu Valley.
“There is no option other than shutting the business if the situation persists for a few more days,” the official said.
Suroj Raj Rajkarnikar, proprietor of Ghangri Café at Jhamsikhel, said his restaurant had only around two cylinders left in stock.
“The dealer from whom we used to get cylinders has stopped supplying,” he said.
Rajkarnikar said his restaurant requires about two cylinders a day.

Bishnu Prasad Dulal, senior vice-president of the Federation of Nepal Gas Distributors, said the LPG supply situation in the Kathmandu Valley would not ease until the Krishnabhir road section reopens.

The road section on the Prithvi Highway has remained closed since last Sunday, disrupting supplies to the valley and pushing up the prices of various goods as the gap between demand and supply widens.

“LPG bottling plants in the Kathmandu Valley are not able to provide sufficient cylinders. The supply is only 5 percent of the total daily demand of 35,000 to 40,000 cylinders. We are struggling,” Dulal said.

Nepal Oil Corporation, in a press statement issued on Sunday, said that until the Prithvi Highway resumes, LPG cylinders would be supplied after being refilled at plants in Tarai districts and transported to Kathmandu through alternative routes.

According to the corporation, 24,494 LPG cylinders of different brands arrived in the Kathmandu Valley through alternative routes last Thursday after being refilled at plants in various Tarai districts. The number increased to 34,134 cylinders on Friday and 29,249 on Saturday.
Despite the alternative arrangements, consumers and businesses say the supplies remain inadequate to meet normal demand in the capital. /dl

articles.title: UN expert Francesca Albanese calls for ‘true paradigm shift’ as Miliband resets policy on Israel
articles.summary:
Exclusive: UN special rapporteur on occupied territories says ban on goods from settlements ‘important’ but must go further if it is to amount to more than a ‘press release’

The UK’s planned…

blocks.text: The UK’s planned ban on trade with unlawful Israeli settlements is a welcome, if overdue, first step and must be judged according to its practical impact, a UN expert has told the Guardian.

The UK foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, has vowed to act more decisively against Israeli settlements, as well as continued restrictions of aid into Gaza, prompting the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, to claim on Saturday that Downing Street was motivated by “Jew hatred”.

Miliband said what he had been told about restriction on aid into Gaza had reinforced the need for more decisive action. But Huckabee, writing on X in support of the Israeli foreign ministry’s own criticisms, said: “The Brits have lost it. The Jew hate of their government knows no boundaries and knows no facts.”

Huckabee did not mention in his statement that Miliband is himself Jewish. The Israeli foreign ministry had said: “Had the foreign secretary been interested in facts rather than stories, he would have known that there are no restrictions whatsoever on bringing medicines into the Gaza Strip, and that no medicine is being blocked.”

Palestinian groups in the UK are holding judgment until they see the fine detail of Miliband’s policy, due to be announced on Tuesday, but are expecting the most significant shift since a previous foreign secretary, David Lammy, withdrew most arms export licences in September 2024.

Speaking to the Guardian, Francesca Albanese, the UN’s special rapporteur on the occupied territories, said a “ban on settlement goods was a change in UK government stance and absolutely important”. She added she would “not join those dismissing it as theatre before the details had been announced”.

She said a settlement trade ban would have to be part of “a true paradigm shift to Israel-Palestine that ultimately seeks to implement the international court of justice advisory opinion in 2024”, which stated that Israel’s presence in the occupied territories was “unlawful in its entirety”. The opinion, she added, said that “all states carry an obligation – not a preference of an obligation – not to recognise the situation as legal, and not render aid and assistance in maintaining it”.

Albanese also said the trade ban could not be narrowly confined to goods – such as agricultural products and cosmetics – since “they are a fraction of what sustains the occupation, and a fraction that Israel can absorb without difficulty”.

The package should also aim to include trade in services, she said, progressively suspending British intelligence cooperation, all arms licensing and the unexamined flights out of RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus. Albanese warned that if the steps were not taken or were “completely off the table”, the changes would “over time come to be seen as not amounting to a reckoning, but a press release”.

She said that a state banning “dates from Ma’ale Adumim [a city in the West Bank]” while “continuing to licence the equipment used to enforce the checkpoints around it” had not “changed its relationship with the occupation … It has rearranged its communication strategy.”

Albanese added that, “because the 2024 ICJ advisory opinion declares the entire Israeli presence in the occupied territories as unlawful, third states’ obligations ‘not to render aid or assistance’ extends to everything that sustains that unlawful presence as a whole.”

blocks.caption: Israeli finance minister Bezalel Smotrich standing near the settlement of Ma’ale Adumim, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, holding a map showing the E1 settlement project. Photograph: Ohad Zwigenberg/AP

blocks.text: Albanese said the UK needed to end any ambiguity around the tender for the E1 settlement that will sever East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank and cut the territory in two, adding: “Since bids close a week before Israel’s elections on 27 October, there is nothing that London can realistically do in September that can change that calendar.”

But she warned the government could not let the tenders simply pass, pointing out that Israel’s finance minister, Bezalel Smotrich, had already said E1 was designed to “bury the idea of a Palestinian state”.

“There is a difference between the tenders closing and the settlement getting built and financed,” she added. “Construction on this scale needs finance, insurance and construction firms, and since E1 amounts to annexation and not just settlement expansion, sanctions or similar have to be threatened against those firms that seek to cooperate with the building of E1.”

Albanese also called on the UK government to join South Africa before the ICJ, and also support Nicaragua on Monday when the ICJ hears preliminary oral objections from Germany over claims filed by the Central American country that Berlin’s continued arms sales to Israel makes it complicit in genocide.

She said: “Britain is not a party to that case. It can still choose which side of the argument it stands on: whether it treats participation in international accountability mechanisms as a threat to an alliance, or recognises that an alliance built on anything other than principle and the rule of law is not an alliance at all. It is an arrangement of convenience, honoured only until convenience changes.”

Finally she urged the UK to issue guidance to UK-based firms not to overcomply with sanctions imposed by the US on the international criminal court prosecutor, the deputy prosecutors, eight judges and an increasing number of others, including herself and Palestinian human rights groups that have cooperated with the court. “This has frozen bank accounts, everywhere, for people doing nothing other than their judicial function or providing evidence lawfully requested by an international court,” she said.

articles.title: VP Sara calls authorities’ actions involving her children ‘child abuse’
articles.summary: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her…

blocks.text: Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, Sept. 7, accused authorities of committing “child abuse” over their alleged presence near locations where her mother and children were staying, saying her family should not be used, threatened or dragged into any pressure against her. In a statement released by the Office of the Vice President (OVP), Duterte said she was particularly concerned about authorities approaching or going to locations where her family members, including minors, were staying. “Ang paglapit o pagpunta sa lugar kung saan naroroon ang aking ina at mga anak, sa kabila ng pag-amin ng DILG Secretary at ng pulisya na alam nila kung nasaan ako dahil sa kanilang surveillance activities, ay isang seryosong usapin, lalo na kung nadadamay o naaapektuhan ang mga menor de edad (Approaching or going to the place where my mother and children are, despite the admission of the DILG secretary and the police that they know where I am because of their surveillance activities, is a serious matter—especially when minors are affected or dragged into the situation),” Duterte said. “Ang mga bata ay hindi dapat ginagamit, tinatakot, o idinadamay sa panggigipit (Children must never be used, threatened, or dragged into harassment),” she said. “Ito ay child abuse (That is child abuse),” she added. READ: https://mb.com.ph/2026/09/05/i-do-not-feel-safe-vp-sara-fears-for-her-life-childrens-safety-after-arrest-warrant Security concerns Duterte said she had previously approached then-Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner Jr. regarding her security, citing the constitutional line of succession. “Dahil ang aking seguridad ay nakaugnay sa Hukbong Sandatahan ng Pilipinas alinsunod sa constitutional line of succession, minabuti kong ipaalam sa dating Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner ang ilang mahahalagang pakiusap (Because my security is linked to the Armed Forces of the Philippines in accordance with the constitutional line of succession, I deemed it necessary to inform former Chief of Staff Gen. Romeo Brawner of several important requests),” Duterte said. “Higit sa lahat, hiniling ko na igalang at protektahan ang aking ina at mga anak, at huwag silang idamay o takutin sa kahit anumang gagawin sa akin (Above all, I asked that my mother and children be respected and protected, and that they not be dragged into or threatened by anything directed at me),” she added. Duterte also lamented that a government that fails to respect and protect children demonstrates a lack of concern for the country’s future. “Mga kababayan, ang isang pamahalaang hindi gumagalang at nagpoprotekta sa mga kabataan ay nagpapakita ng kawalan ng malasakit sa kinabukasan ng ating bayan (Fellow citizens, a government that does not respect and protect children reveals a lack of concern for the future of our nation),” Duterte said. Alleged plans date back to 2024 Duterte also claimed that she had received information as early as 2024 about alleged plans involving her and her father, former President Rodrigo Duterte. “Taong 2024 pa lamang ay umabot na sa akin ang impormasyon ng mga planong gawin ni Marcos (As early as 2024, information about Marcos’ plans had already reached me),” Duterte said. “Matagal na ako sa pampublikong serbisyo at nakahanda ako araw-araw sa posibilidad gawa ng aking trabaho (I have long been in public service, and I am prepared each day for the possibilities that come with my work),” she added. Duterte said the alleged plans included an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for her father and attacks against her. “Kabilang sa mga plano ang magkaroon ng ICC warrant kay dating Pangulong Duterte at ang mga gagawin na pag-atake sa akin (Among the plans were the issuance of an ICC warrant against former President Duterte and attacks directed at me),” she said. Surveillance allegations Duterte’s latest accusation followed her Sept. 5 allegations that the Marcos administration had been conducting surveillance and harassment operations against her and her family. She cited remarks from Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla, who said authorities knew her whereabouts the night before an arrest warrant was issued but did not immediately enforce it. Duterte said Remulla’s statement appeared to support documents she claimed her camp had long held regarding alleged surveillance and harassment operations by the Philippine National Police (PNP) and other government agencies. She also questioned why authorities allegedly went to her mother and children if government agencies already knew her whereabouts. “And because you know where I am, an important question you should answer is—why did you still need to go to my mother and children?” she said. She alleged that the purpose was to intimidate her family. “Isa lamang ang malinaw na sagot—upang takutin at sindakin ang aking pamilya (There is only one clear answer—to frighten and intimidate my family),” Duterte said. Duterte also said she did not trust the police and maintained that she could not surrender to authorities because she did not believe the government could guarantee her safety while in custody. She invoked the arrest and transfer of her father to the custody of the ICC, which she characterized as a “kidnapping” by the PNP. Duterte’s allegations come amid continuing political and legal tensions between her camp and the administration of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., including disputes involving law enforcement, her family and legal proceedings. articles.title: Jonvic: Plan to 'dramatize' VP Sara arrest prevented
articles.summary: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of…

blocks.text: Police prevented the alleged plot to exploit the service of the arrest warrant against Vice President Sara Duterte through what a ranking official described as a planned drama that includes images of her in handcuffs and inside a detention facility. Duterte was issued with an arrest warrant by a Quezon City Regional Trial Court for a case of grave threats and Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Jonvic Remulla said the plan was to make it appear that the Vice President was being treated unfairly. “Ang drama nila gusto nila makulong siya, at naka-hand-cuff siya. The high drama na dapat makulong siya agad dito. (Their drama is that they want her behind bars and in handcuffs. The high drama that she should be jailed here (Camp Crame) right away,” said Remulla in a press briefing. “Hindi kami pumayag (We did not agree). We wanted to go according to the rules to the rues of law and to the rules of court and we accorded her the respect that her positions deserve,” she added. The Department of Justice filed charges of grave threats against Duterte in connection with the assassination threat she allegedly said in an online discussion with vloggers—threats directed to President Marcos, First Lady Liza Araneta Marcos, and former House speaker Martin Romualdez. On Friday, Sept. 4, the QC RTC Branch 98 issued an arrest warrant against her. The following day, Duterte arrived at the QC RTC to post bail. It was then that Durerte was quoted accusing the PNP of harassment, and remarked that she fear for her life and that she does not trust the court and the police. The truth according to the PNP Both Remulla and the Philippine National Police (PNP), through the Criminal Investigation and Detection Group (CIDG), denied the allegation of harassment and surveillance. In a press briefing on Monday, Sept. 7, CIDG director Maj. Gen. Robert Alexander Morico narrated what actually happened the moment they received the arrest warrant from the Branch 98 of the QC RTC. He said the CIDG received the arrest warrant at 12:45 p.m. and immediately, a team from the unit’s Women and Children Protection Desk proceeded to Mandaluyong City where the Vice President is holding office to inform her camp of the court’s order. “We have coordinated with the Vice President Security Group because the subject of the warrant of arrest is the second highest official of the land and we know that there are security arrangements for the President and the Vice President,” said Morico. Morico said they have been in constant coordination with Duterte’s security officer in relation to the service of the arrest warrant and her camp, sent a certain Major Nabua to personally coordinate. The initial arrangement According to Morico, there were already negotiations between the CIDG and the Vice President Security Group since the issuance of the arrest warrant on Friday—and part of that coordination was the visit of the certain Major Nabua whom he said, interestingly asked where the Vice President would be detained inside Camp Crame. “I told him that there is still time for the Vice President to post bail because it’s a bailable offense, that we can escort her after all the booking procedures to the QC RTC to post bail,” said Morico. Morico said they were later told that the Vice President did not want to post bail. “But I was informed of the VSPG that she does not want to post bail. She wants to be incarcerated so they asked where is the jail facility,” said Morico. ‘I told the Major Nabua and his commanding officer that I will not commit the Vice President to jail facilities. She will be placed to conference room because we have to afford her the necessary respect due to her office,” he stressed. Of Jollibee and McDo Morico said they could not commit Duterte to any jail facility because they are full of notorious criminals and that the main detention facilities are undergoing renovation. The most that the CIDG could do, according to her, is to accommodate her to the CIDG conference room with some amenities that include a folding bed and the most expensive meal that the police could afford—from Jollibee and Mc Donald. “But we told them that they can bring food,” said Morico. Change of mind According to Morico, he said they waited until 1 a.m. the following day but did not show up. Instead, he said they were informed that the Vice President would go to QC Regional Trial Court instead to post bail. “So I dispatched a team to the house of the Vice President in San Juan to escort her. No need for armed unit because she has her own coming from the VSPG,” said Morico.

articles.title: San Lazaro Hospital reports downward trend in leptospirosis admissions
articles.summary: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on…

blocks.text: Leptospirosis admissions at San Lazaro Hospital are on a downward trend, with the daily count dropping to four on Monday, Sept. 7. The hospital recorded its highest daily admission count at 50 on Aug. 26, after which admissions declined before rising again to 40 on Sept. 3. The number then dropped to 23 on Sept. 5, 13 on Sept. 6, and four on Sept. 7. More patients were also discharged than admitted over the past two days, with 32 patients discharged on Sept. 6 and 34 on Sept. 7. Monitoring continues following the Aug. 17 and 29 flooding in Metro Manila brought by the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” which may have exposed residents to contaminated floodwaters. Leptospirosis is associated with exposure to water or soil contaminated with the urine of infected animals. San Lazaro Hospital advised the public to avoid wading in floodwaters and to wash with clean water and soap after possible exposure. People are also advised to keep their surroundings clean and free from rodents, drink safe water, and eat well-cooked food. Those exposed to contaminated floodwaters should watch for symptoms such as fever, headache, muscle pain, and jaundice and seek immediate medical attention if they develop them. articles.title: Free Legal Consultation Service Expanding for Japanese Abroad
articles.summary: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japan's Foreign Ministry is working to expand a support system that allows Japanese nationals and their families abroad who have become victims of crimes to consult local…

blocks.text: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japan's Foreign Ministry is working to expand a support system that allows Japanese nationals and their families abroad who have become victims of crimes to consult local lawyers free of charge.

The initiative was first introduced in China last year and has since been launched in the Philippines and Thailand. The ministry aims to make the service available in more and more countries, particularly focusing on nations with many incidents and large numbers of consultations.

The system was established in the wake of an incident in which a Japanese boy was stabbed to death in the Chinese city of Shenzhen in September 2024. As the bereaved family faced difficulties navigating legal procedures that differ from those in Japan, the ministry began to consider offering Japanese-language lawyer consultations and launched the program in China in January 2025.

The ministry assumes that the service is available mainly to victims of serious crimes such as murder, bodily injury, assault, domestic violence, nonconsensual sexual intercourse and indecent assault. Those seeking assistance can apply through a Japanese diplomatic mission abroad to receive from lawyers explanations on how to submit victim reports and on investigation and trial procedures, as well as advice on seeking damages and compensation.
“The number of consultations is increasing, and there is demand," a government official said.
Due to budget constraints, however, free consultations are limited to three sessions per case. A list of local lawyers will be provided upon request.

The initiative was rolled out in the Philippines in May this year and in Thailand last month. The launch in the two Southeast Asian countries was prompted by a shooting incident in the Philippines in August 2025 that killed two Japanese nationals and the fact that Thailand recorded the highest number of incidents in 2025 in which government support was provided.
“Criminal cases are especially common in Asia," a senior Foreign Ministry official said.

Crimes and accidents involving Japanese citizens as victims have been prevalent in recent years. In 2025, Japanese nationals received government support in 12,239 cases abroad. Of the total, 5,633 cases were in Asia, with 705 involving crime victims.
“Awareness of the system is still low," a Foreign Ministry official said. "We want victims, including those of domestic violence and sexual assault, to consult Japanese diplomatic missions first."

articles.title: Balisacan: AI can fight corruption, monitor projects, speed up government
articles.summary: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance…

blocks.text: The Marcos Jr. administration plans to harness artificial intelligence (AI) to streamline government processes, monitor infrastructure projects, and help fight corruption as it prepares a governance framework for the rapidly evolving technology, according to the country ’s chief economist. Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) Secretary Arsenio M. Balisacan told reporters last week that AI could be deployed across critical public sectors, including education, health, and infrastructure, to improve government efficiency and accelerate the delivery of public services. Balisacan identified project monitoring as among the most practical applications of AI, particularly in tracking infrastructure development and ensuring projects are completed on time. The DEPDev chief said AI could also be applied to public-private partnership (PPP) projects. He said automating government processes through AI could also strengthen efforts against corruption. The AI governance framework is “more or less finished,” Balisacan said, with its formal release possibly this month, depending on President Ferdinand R. Marcos Jr.’s schedule. He said the President could still propose changes to make the framework more workable and flexible as the government seeks to use AI as a tool for development. The framework builds on the National AI Strategy of the Philippines (NAIS-PH), which the government approved in May 2025. The government’s push to integrate AI into its operations forms part of a broader effort to harness the technology to raise productivity and support economic development while preparing Filipino workers and industries for the disruptions it could bring. Balisacan earlier said fears that AI could cause massive job losses in the country’s information technology and business process management (IT-BPM) industry may be overstated, as the sector continues to expand despite the rapid adoption of the technology. Speaking at the Economic Journalists Association of the Philippines (EJAP) Economic Forum last month, Balisacan identified innovation and productivity as major sources of economic growth and stressed the need to upskill the Filipino workforce to adapt to emerging technologies such as AI. The DEPDev chief also pointed to the proposed Pax Silica development in New Clark City as an opportunity to diversify the economy by attracting investments that support industrialization and higher-value activities. The government, however, faces challenges in building the foundations needed to maximize the economic benefits of AI. Manila Bulletin reported earlier the World Bank ’s warning that weak and fragmented data systems could hold back the country’s AI ambitions and recommended the formulation of a cohesive government data strategy identifying the investments needed in data, infrastructure, and people. The proposed strategy could form part of the data pillar of the AI governance framework being developed under the National Innovation Council (NIC), with DEPDev among the lead agencies. Beyond government operations, Balisacan has identified potential AI applications in the energy sector to optimize power grids while promoting greener and more efficient operations. He also sees AI-enabled assistive technologies playing a role in healthcare and social inclusion as the country’s population ages. Balisacan has also stressed the importance of expanding the country’s digital infrastructure through initiatives such as eGovPH, the national fiber backbone, satellite internet, and the Konektadong Pinoy Act. He has likewise emphasized the need for ethical and trustworthy AI use, including adherence to Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT)-Civil Service Commission (CSC) guidelines on responsible AI use in government to uphold transparency and accountability.

articles.title: Nepal: The flood is over, the fear remains
articles.summary: KATHMANDU — Sixteen-year-old Samiksha Dangol was on her way home from school when she saw her father coming towards her. It was the morning of August 26 at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School…

blocks.text: KATHMANDU — Sixteen-year-old Samiksha Dangol was on her way home from school when she saw her father coming towards her.

It was the morning of August 26 at Tribhuvan Trishuli Secondary School in Nuwakot, a district north-west of Kathmandu. Samikshya, a Grade 11 student, had been sent home after the school received warnings that floodwaters were rising.
Her father had come to take her home.
But the two did not get far. A traffic police officer stopped them and warned that the flood was rising and that they should not cross the bridge.
They waited, assuming the rest of the family had already fled.
They had not.
When Samiksha and her father learnt what had happened, both collapsed.
Her older sister, brother and two aunts (father’s sisters) were missing in the flood.
Days later, after staying at a temporary holding centre, Samiksha moved to her maternal relatives’ home. The water has receded, but August 26 keeps returning to her.
She struggles to sleep. Memories of playing with her siblings surface without warning. She cries and feels restless.
“I tell myself to forget it,” she said. “But I keep thinking about my sister and brothers. The things we did together keep playing in my mind.”

The physical effects have been difficult too. Samiksha, who already suffers from migraines, became so unwell that she and her mother had to be taken to hospital. The family had lost so much that even the medicine she normally took was unavailable.

For children like Samiksha, the disaster did not end when the floodwaters fell. Across Nuwakot, Rasuwa and neighboring districts, children who survived the floods, witnessed destruction or lost relatives are now confronting a less visible aftermath: fear. Some wake in the middle of night. Some become withdrawn. Others panic at sounds that remind them of the disaster.
In Rasuwa, Karsang Tamang’s 21-month-old son becomes frightened whenever he hears a loud noise.
On August 26, Karsang grabbed her sleeping son and ran as floodwaters swept through the area around Timure, Rasuwa. People were screaming and running in panic.
Since then, even the sound of a helicopter can make the toddler cry.
“He had never been like this before,” Karsang said. “Now he gets startled and frightened from time to time. When he panics, it causes me a lot of pain too.”
Karsang is sheltering at Yellow Gumba (Buddhist monastery) in western Kathmandu. She is more worried about her young son than about what she herself endured.
The scale of the impact on children is difficult to measure.

UNICEF estimates that 17,000 children have been affected by the floods in Nepal. Data from Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority show that 6,901 students at 19 schools in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading were affected. Local education offices, municipalities and schools estimate that 622 students in Rasuwa and Nuwakot alone remain unaccounted for following the Bhotekoshi flooding.

The numbers capture the scale of the disaster. They do not capture what it feels like for a child to hear a helicopter and be taken back to the moment they ran for safety, or to close their eyes and see a missing sibling.
Some children were found after spending hours or days trapped by the flood.

A six-year-old girl rescued from Timure on August 28 was among them. An Armed Police Force search team heard what sounded like a child crying and followed the sound. They found her injured and brought her to Kathmandu, where she is receiving treatment at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital.
Her mother, Geeta Magar, said the girl barely spoke during the first days in hospital.
“She would just keep looking at me,” Magar said. Doctors told the family that the child appeared to have forgotten some things after the flood and had also developed pneumonia.
For aid workers who arrived at temporary shelters, the change in the children was immediately visible.

At the holding centre at Chandrajyoti Secondary School in Devighat, Nuwakot, Nepal Scouts volunteer Hritik Magiya saw children who were initially too frightened or withdrawn to participate in even simple activities.
“When we first came here, the children were in a very different state,” he said. “They were very sad and afraid, wondering what to do if another flood came.”
Some had lost parents or other relatives. Others were waiting for family members who had not yet been found.
In the first days, Magiya said, many children would sit apart from the group. Even when volunteers organised games, some refused to join.
“They were quiet and did not participate in any activities,” he said.
That response is not unusual after a disaster, mental health specialists say.
Psychiatrist Dr Amit Jha said children can be particularly vulnerable because they have fewer resources than adults to understand and regulate fear and stress.

After a disaster, children may have difficulty sleeping, experience a racing heartbeat, sweating or rapid breathing. Such symptoms can form part of an acute stress reaction. If they continue for several weeks, they may develop into anxiety or depressive disorders. In some cases, particularly among children who directly experienced the disaster or lost relatives, prolonged trauma can develop into post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD).
The psychological impact can extend beyond children who were physically caught in the floods.

Children elsewhere may also be affected after repeatedly watching footage of floods and landslides on television or social media, Jha said. Repeated exposure to distressing images and accounts can leave children frightened, anxious or restless even if they were nowhere near the disaster.
For that reason, adults should be careful about what children see and hear, he said, particularly in the immediate aftermath.
The challenge facing Nepal now is to prevent an emergency response from becoming another source of trauma.
For children who have lost parents or guardians, the stakes are especially high.

“There are many children who have lost their father, mother or guardians,” said Geeta KC Darnal, a child protection officer with Sahayatri Nepal. “We cannot fully understand the pain of losing a parent at such a young age. The immediate priority is to help them come out of the trauma.”
Government agencies and aid organizations have begun providing psychological and psychosocial support.

The National Child Rights Council says it is coordinating with volunteers, counsellors, doctors and local authorities working in affected areas. “The council is also collecting information on the number of children killed and affected in the disaster,” Ram Bahadur Chand, an information officer at the council, said.

Bidur Municipality, meanwhile, says medical teams from all three levels of government are providing mental health and psychosocial counselling. Child-focussed organizations have also established services at holding centers.

The municipality is preparing residential arrangements for children who have been separated from their families or otherwise left without adequate care. Two residential schools have been selected to accommodate some of them.
At the holding centre, officials and aid workers have also tried to give children space to play and return, as much as possible, to familiar routines.
That can be more important than it sounds.
Magiya said the children at the Devighat centre gradually became more engaged after volunteers spent time with them, played games, and told stories.

“We gradually involved them in different activities while also feeding them,” he said. “We played games with them on the school grounds, spent time with them and told them stories. We also asked them to sketch and draw with coloured pencils.”
The children who had initially avoided the volunteers eventually began approaching them on their own.
Some now remember the volunteers’ names, play with them and talk to them.
Yet children who lost relatives still become visibly sad from time to time.
The recovery, experts say, will not be measured simply by whether children return to school or leave temporary shelters. Trauma can emerge slowly.
Milan Dharel, a former executive director of the National Child Rights Council, said the effects of disasters can be physical, psychological and socio-economic.

There is another danger: children who lose the protection of their families can become vulnerable to trafficking, child labour, violence and abuse. Dharel warned that even efforts presented as protection can become mechanisms for exploitation.
The risk has become particularly visible on social media, where images and videos of children affected by the floods have circulated.

Offers to take children in or raise them may appear sympathetic, but child protection officials urge caution. Children can also be exploited through fundraising, online content, or institutions claiming to provide shelter, Dharel said.

The government, he said, has two immediate responsibilities: ensuring that search-and-rescue operations remain child-sensitive, and monitoring anyone who assumes responsibility for a child separated from their family.
Authorities have also warned against another form of harm: turning children’s suffering into public content.

The National Child Rights Council and Nepal Police have urged the public and media not to publish photographs, videos, or personal information that could identify children affected by the floods. Such exposure can violate their privacy and dignity and cause lasting harm to their mental health.
For children already carrying memories of homes swept away, relatives disappearing and adults screaming in fear, the recovery may depend on more than rebuilding roads or bridges.
Psychiatrist Jha calls the first response “psychological first aid”.
Children need to feel safe, he said, adding, adults should reassure them that they are protected, rather than repeatedly asking them to recount what happened.
Parents can help where they are present. Where parents have died or remain missing, relatives, communities and the state must take their place.
The most useful response can be remarkably simple: stay with the child, listen and allow them to speak when they are ready, Jha said.
Children should also be helped back into ordinary life as soon as circumstances permit, including a return to school.

The floods have left the country with damaged infrastructure, disrupted communities and families still searching for those who have not returned. But for children such as Samiksha, the disaster continues to affect daily life. She still struggles to sleep and is often reminded of her siblings and the things they did together. /dl

articles.title: Kumamoto Quake Victims Begin Moving into Temporary Housing
articles.summary: Hikawa, Kumamoto Pref., Sept. 5 (Jiji Press)--Residents of the town of Hikawa in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, whose homes were damaged in a massive earthquake in late July began moving…

blocks.text: Hikawa, Kumamoto Pref., Sept. 5 (Jiji Press)--Residents of the town of Hikawa in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, whose homes were damaged in a massive earthquake in late July began moving into emergency temporary housing Saturday. A total of 20 makeshift housing units were built in the town, which experienced shaking of 7, the highest level on the Japanese seismic intensity scale, in the 7.1-magnitude quake around 4:27 p.m. on July 28. They are the first temporary housing made available in the prefecture after the earthquake. A ceremony to hand over keys to the housing units was held from around 9 a.m. Saturday, with Kumamoto Governor Takashi Kimura and Hikawa Mayor KazuomiFujimoto in attendance. Attendees observed a moment of silence for quake victims. "We will do all we can for reconstruction so that all residents can regain their normal lives as soon as possible," Fujimoto said in an address. Kimura vowed to provide solid support in cooperation with the town. Takahiro Miyagawa, 73, who received the keys on behalf of the new residents, had lived in a relative's house since the quake, which completely destroyed his home. "I'm relieved that I can finally move in," he told reporters. "We'll make a fresh start." The 20 single-story emergency homes made with lightweight steel frames stand on the site of a former town-run housing complex, with 15 of them having two rooms and a kitchen and the other five with three rooms and a kitchen. Evacuees will be able to live in the temporary homes for up to two years in principle. Similar homes are being built in the Kumamoto cities of Uki and Yatsushiro, which also suffered extensive damage from the temblor. According to the Kumamoto prefectural government, fatalities from the earthquake stood at 38 as of 2 p.m. Friday, including two whose deaths were suspected to have been indirectly caused by the disaster. A total of 64,903 residential buildings were damaged, including 1,748 that were completely destroyed. The temblor struck about 10 years after Kumamoto was hit by two powerful earthquakes in April 2016, which also measured up to 7 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale.

articles.title: Antonelli charges from back to win epic Italian GP
articles.summary: MONZA, Italy (AP) — Kimi Antonelli took a big step to becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history with a fightback for the ages at his home grand prix on Sunday, Sept. 6. Antonelli stormed to…

blocks.text: MONZA, Italy (AP) — Kimi Antonelli took a big step to becoming the youngest champion in Formula 1 history with a fightback for the ages at his home grand prix on Sunday, Sept. 6. Antonelli stormed to victory at the Italian Grand Prix, despite having started 19th on the grid. It took the Mercedes driver fewer than 17 laps to fight his way to the front. The rest of the race was spent tussling with teammate and title rival George Russell for the lead. Antonelli passed him for the final time with three laps remaining, going on to become the first Italian to win at Monza in 60 years. “Oh my God ... It feels like a dream,” Antonelli said on team radio after crossing the line. ‘Unbelievable, unbelievable’ “I did not expect it," Antonelli said later. “Unbelievable, unbelievable. I am so happy, I could not have imagined to be here today but we managed to pull it off and I am really, really happy.” It was the second furthest back anyone has come from to win a grand prix. John Watson won at Long Beach in 1983 despite starting 22nd. “The best (race) is yet to come. But I feel like it was one of the best races I've done so far and one that I will remember forever,” said the 20-year-old Antonelli, who is in his second season in F1. Antonelli’s triumph at least gave the crowd something to cheer about after Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc crashed out of the scuderia’s home race early on. In the other Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton finished sixth. Max Verstappen was a distant third behind the two Mercedes, just ahead of the McLaren duo of defending champion Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. It was Antonelli’s seventh win of the season — and his fledgling F1 career — and extended his lead in the overall standings to 66 points ahead of Russell. Russell had been hoping to make up some ground on Antonelli in the title race as his teammate took on a hefty grid penalty at Monza after Mercedes opted to swap his car’s power unit. “Kimi is in control of it and he’s deserving to be in control of it,” Russell said about the title race. "For me personally, I’m not even thinking about a fight or a comeback or anything. “He’s performing incredibly well. It’s going to be exceptionally challenging to overcome that gap so I’m just sort of accepting that it is what it is.” Fans in tears Russel started Sunday's grand prix second and got ahead of surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly at the start of the second lap. Moments later the race was red-flagged after Leclerc lost control coming out of Parabolica at the end of Lap 2 and swerved off into the barriers at high speed. He got out of his car and sat down near the track, looking heartbroken. The hordes of passionate, red-clad tifosi around the track looked similarly despondent, with many in tears. By that point Antonelli was already up to 12th and — as he later admitted — starting to believe in victory. When the race resumed, he continued to slice swiftly through the field, picking off the cars one by one until he only had Russell ahead. No yo-yo The Mercedes duo were told off by their team as they yo-yoed for the lead and instructed to build a gap over Verstappen before fighting it out for the victory. Antonelli was brought into the pits under the virtual safety car on lap 29, while Russell stayed out. Antonelli came out in sixth but, with fresh tires, started reeling Russell in for the second time in the race. “To be honest, I thought we were both going to stay out,” Russell said. "I was surprised to see him pitting. "In the end it was a roll of the dice both ways. In the moment, the team wouldn’t have known which strategy was better, made sense to split the car. In the end Kimi had great pace.” Antonelli looked as though he may have blown his chances of a stunning comeback win when he ran through the gravel as he attempted to get past Russell on Lap 49. But such was his pace that he soon closed the gap that had opened up and breezed past the following lap.

articles.title: Japanese Prince Hisahito Turns 20, Leading Fulfilling Life
articles.summary: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japanese Prince Hisahito, the son of Crown Prince Akishino and Crown Princess Kiko, turned 20 on Sunday, leading a fulfilling life mainly through his studies at…

blocks.text: Tokyo, Sept. 6 (Jiji Press)--Japanese Prince Hisahito, the son of Crown Prince Akishino and Crown Princess Kiko, turned 20 on Sunday, leading a fulfilling life mainly through his studies at university. The prince, second in line to the throne, is a second-year student of the College of Biological Sciences in the School of Life and Environmental Sciences at the University of Tsukuba, and is also engaging in official duties as a young member of the Imperial Family. After completing his coming-of-age ceremony in September last year, Prince Hisahito made his debut at several events at the Imperial Palace, such as the New Year's greetings in early January and a banquet for Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and his wife held during their state visit to Japan in May. For the Imperial New Year's poetry-reading ceremony, known as "utakai hajime," he submitted a poem for the first time, depicting a memory related to dragonflies, a subject of his research. In the past year, the prince visited six prefectures--Hokkaido, northernmost Japan, Mie in central Japan, and Kyoto, Osaka, Nara and Hiroshima in western Japan. Last month, he attended a boy scout event in Hiroshima unaccompanied by other Imperial Family members. He worked with other participants around his age to prepare "tonjiru" pork miso soup for breakfast, chatting in a friendly manner with them while checking the fire for the pot containing the ingredients. Last November, he visited the remote Tokyo island of Izu Oshima in the Pacific with his mother to watch an orienteering event of the Tokyo Deaflympics. He high-fived children who came to see him off at a port on the island. At the University of Tsukuba, located in the city of Tsukuba, Ibaraki Prefecture, northeast of Tokyo, Prince Hisahito is taking compulsory courses in English, which helps him read biology papers, and physical education, according to an aide. His biology-related courses and lab classes have become more advanced, and he took part in an outdoor field study this summer. He now spends most of his time in the city of Tsukuba. When he is at his family's residence at the Akasaka Estate in Tokyo, he often grows vegetables and rice, and observes dragonflies. The prince has been deeply interested in maps since childhood. Last month, he visited the Geospatial Information Authority of Japan's Science Museum of Map and Survey near his university and deepened his knowledge of Japan's geological features and surveying. The prince mourned the victims of recent natural disasters, including a major earthquake in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan, in July and torrential rains in many parts of the country, while wishing all those affected well.

articles.title: Mark Villar seeks hazard pay, extra insurance for media workers deployed to dangerous assignments
articles.summary: Senator Mark Villar is pushing for additional protection for media workers who are deployed to hazardous locations, filing a measure that would provide them with hazard pay and expanded insurance…

blocks.text: Senator Mark Villar is pushing for additional protection for media workers who are deployed to hazardous locations, filing a measure that would provide them with hazard pay and expanded insurance coverage while carrying out dangerous assignments. Villar filed Senate Bill No. 2440, or the proposed “Media Workers Hazard Pay Act,” which seeks to provide financial and insurance benefits to accredited media personnel assigned to areas affected by armed conflict, disasters, disease outbreaks, and other emergency situations. “Media workers serve as the eyes and ears of the public during the most difficult and dangerous situations. Kung inaasahan natin silang humarap sa panganib upang mapanatiling ligtas at may sapat na kaalaman ang ating mga kababayan, tungkulin din nating tiyakin na sila ay protektado, insured, at makatarungang binabayaran,” Villar said. The senator pointed to previous incidents involving journalists who encountered serious risks while performing their duties. Among them was a television reporter who spent nearly two weeks in the hospital in 2022 after contracting leptospirosis while covering an incident in Payatas, Quezon City. Another reporter assigned to provide weather updates in 2024 also found himself affected by flooding in his own community and struggled to protect his belongings. Under Villar's proposal, accredited media workers from both government and private-sector organizations would qualify for a minimum hazard pay of ₱650 per day when their duties require them to physically report from dangerous areas. These would include conflict-affected or embattled locations, isolated or distressed stations, areas affected by infectious diseases, and places placed under a state of calamity or emergency. The additional pay would cover the entire period of the hazardous assignment and could not be lowered. However, employees who already receive hazard compensation equal to or greater than the proposed amount would not receive a separate benefit under the measure. The bill would also compel employers to provide additional insurance protection to covered media workers. The proposed package includes a ₱200,000 death benefit for those who die while performing their duties, as well as disability compensation of up to ₱200,000 for total or partial disability caused by injuries sustained in the line of duty. Medical insurance coverage of up to ₱100,000 would also be provided to each covered worker. Villar's proposal further seeks additional compensation for media personnel required to work beyond the standard eight-hour shift or during the 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. period, subject to existing laws and accepted industry practices. The senator said the benefits are necessary given the risks routinely faced by journalists and other media personnel, including reporters, camera operators, and technical staff, particularly when covering disasters and other emergencies. According to Villar, media workers play an important role in delivering verified information, government warnings, disaster preparedness instructions, and emergency contact numbers to communities during crises. “Behind every live report from a flooded community, conflict area, or disease-infested location is a media worker who chooses to fulfill his or her duty despite the risks. Their courage and public service must be recognized through concrete and enforceable benefits,” Villar said.

articles.title: Empty seats, tired stars: The US Open’s post-2 a.m. finishes spark a pushback
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Alexander Zverev wasn’t in the mood for much conversation. With empty seats everywhere after he finished his U.S. Open first-round match in the early morning hours, he took two…

blocks.text: NEW YORK (AP) — Alexander Zverev wasn’t in the mood for much conversation. With empty seats everywhere after he finished his U.S. Open first-round match in the early morning hours, he took two questions from reporters on the court and quickly wrapped it up. “I think everybody’s tired," he said. “Everybody wants to go to sleep.” The city that never sleeps is going a little overboard this year. Players have long loved the electricity of night matches at the U.S. Open, where tennis under the lights at Arthur Ashe Stadium is a hallmark of the American Grand Slam tournament, with fans staying late and bringing plenty of energy. But with the tournament this year already setting a record with three post-2 a.m. finishes over the first six days, plus two more going past 1 a.m., concerns are bubbling up about how much after midnight is too much on such a big stage. “I know they’re dealing with a lot of different aspects as far as broadcast and TV and making sure certain matches get done and are starting at a certain time for those reasons,” third-ranked women's player Jessica Pegula said. ”But you have to wonder if it’s really the right thing for players to be finishing at 2 a.m., especially when it’s not — like, I’m not watching on TV. I’m sleeping. Some people stay, but there is a lot of people that need to go home.” Wimbledon instituted an 11 p.m. curfew. The French Open schedules just one match a night. The U.S. Open is famous for going late, though this time maybe to an extreme. On opening night, Venus Williams was subjected to the latest start in U.S. Open history at 12:13 a.m., after it took 4 hours, 36 minutes for Novak Djokovic to get knocked out in the first round. Much of the crowd stuck around to see what could wind up being the 46-year-old's final Grand Slam singles match, a loss to Sofia Kenin, but the timing itself was a challenge. “It’s not ideal,” Williams said. “I would have preferred something else, definitely. It wasn’t great for either of us, so I think we both tried our best. I just don’t know any other sport where you have to start that late. I definitely think there’s room for improvement there." Zverev's first two matches ended at 1:55 and 2:15 a.m., making him the first top-seeded man to play back-to-back five-set matches to start a major in the Open era, which dates to 1968. Ben Shelton's second-rounder that started Friday night went until 2:07 a.m. Saturday thanks to the Williams sisters' doubles match lasting more than three hours. Four of the latest 17 finishes in tournament history have occurred this year. The record is still 2:50 a.m. from when Carlos Alcaraz beat Jannik Sinner in the quarterfinals in 2022 on the way to his first U.S. Open title. "Not easy," Shelton said after defeating Denis Shapovalov in 3 hours, 22 minutes. “My first time experiencing playing this late.” Shelton figured the earliest he'd get to sleep was 5 a.m. Top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka, who two years ago played what is now the fourth-latest women's match, is not a fan of playing after midnight and the potentially lingering effects. “When you finish late, the next day shifts a lot,” Sabalenka said. “Like, you still need to get your hours of sleep, so you start later. You just can really mess up your schedule.”

Infantino has faced increasing pressure after his controversial plan to sell stakes in the World Cup was met with a furious backlash. UEFA, European soccer's governing body, has led the calls for Infantino to go, saying it had lost confidence in him and previously threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments, including the World Cup. A number of national associations, such the English FA, have withdrawn support for Infantino's re-election. On Saturday Infantino refused to comment about his future when arriving for the opening of the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland. “There will be a lot to say, but there will be a right place and a right time to say this. It’s not today, it’s not here, but here and today, we are enjoying football,” he told Sky News. FIFA apologized for errors made over its controversial plan to sell profits in the World Cup through a commercial subsidiary and committed to “ensure they do not happen again.” But that hasn't been enough to ease the pressure on Infantino's position. UEFA is preparing a criminal complaint against Infantino in Swiss courts for possible financial mismanagement over his now abandoned plan to sell future World Cup profits to private investors. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham added his weight to the debate last month, saying Infantino was not the right man to lead world soccer’s governing body.

articles.title: Manila declares leptospirosis epidemic
articles.summary: Manila has declared a leptospirosis epidemic after cases rose beyond the city’s set danger level, with several city-run hospitals now reaching full capacity amid the continued influx of patients. "We…

blocks.text: Manila has declared a leptospirosis epidemic after cases rose beyond the city’s set danger level, with several city-run hospitals now reaching full capacity amid the continued influx of patients. "We surpass the epidemic threshold for leptospirosis," the city government announced. Manila OIC-City Health Officer Dr. Grace Padilla reported the development to Mayor Francisco “Isko” Moreno Domagoso on Monday, Sept. 7, saying the city is now in an “epidemic condition” due to the rising number of leptospirosis cases. Based on data from the Manila Health Department (MHD), the city’s attack rate for leptospirosis jumped to 3.48 percent from 1.27 percent last week, indicating a rapid increase in cases within a short period. Padilla also reported that several city government district hospitals have reached full capacity due to the continued influx of patients. These include Ospital ng Maynila, Sta. Ana Hospital, and Justice Jose Abad Santos General Hospital. Following the report, Domagoso directed city government agencies to intensify the city’s campaign against leptospirosis, particularly among residents who were exposed to floodwaters in recent weeks. The city government will also step up its public information campaign to inform residents that free doxycycline capsules are available at all 44 health centers and seven district hospitals under the Manila city government. Domagoso said the city government, through the MHD and its 896 barangays, should proactively reach out to residents affected by flooding and distribute doxycycline to those exposed to floodwaters. He stressed that it would be better for the city government to bring the preventive medicine directly to affected residents as leptospirosis cases continue to rise.

articles.title: Reigning champions Sabalenka, Alcaraz storm into US Open quarters
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Defending champions Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz are back to the quarterfinals at the U.S. Open, and they made it look easy. The top-ranked Sabalenka solved some early struggles…

blocks.text: NEW YORK (AP) — Defending champions Aryna Sabalenka and Carlos Alcaraz are back to the quarterfinals at the U.S. Open, and they made it look easy. The top-ranked Sabalenka solved some early struggles holding serve and overpowered Taylor Townsend, 6-4, 6-3, on Sunday, Sept. 6. Alcaraz also advanced in straight sets, beating Tommy Paul, 6-4, 6-3, 6-4, in the second match at Arthur Ashe Stadium. “I'm happy with that performance,” Alcaraz said. “I played my game. I tried to play my style. Tommy’s such a talented player. His shots are pretty dangerous and it's sometimes pretty difficult to control the ball when it comes to you, so I just tried to be ready.” Townsend broke Sabalenka three times in her first four service games as she looked to spring the upset. Sabalenka found a groove, regained her confidence and did not lose another point after falling behind 3-1 in the second set. “I love matches like that because it was really challenging," Sabalenka said. “Going through tough challenges and overcoming those challenges, it definitely gives you strength and really strong belief that you can do it.” This was the first meeting between Sabalenka and Townsend, who gave her opponent fits in the first set but struggled to find her own rhythm. “This was the most comfortable and confident I’ve ever been playing against a No. 1 player in the world,” Townsend said. “From the beginning, I felt like I belonged. From the beginning, I felt like I was right where I needed to be. I still feel that way.” Next up for Sabalenka is Wimbledon winner Linda Noskova, who needed six match points to get past Marta Kostyuk 7-5, 5-7, 6-4. "I played a couple of matches against her in the past, which also wasn’t the easiest matches," Sabalenka said of Noskova. “Really aggressive style of the game. Serving really well, playing super fast. You’ve got to stay really low to be able to handle that power and energy.” Alcaraz cruises into the quarterfinals Playing his first tournament following a four-month absence because of a right wrist injury, Alcaraz said last week he would not be coming back if he could not play like his usual self. The 23-year-old Spaniard has made good on that so far, dropping just one set through four rounds. Alcaraz dictated play on the way to extending his Grand Slam winning streak to 18. When Paul was making things interesting in the third set, Alcaraz set up match point by hitting a shot so perfectly in bounds that it left actor Matthew McConaughey in disbelief, along with many others in the crowd. Asked if he thinks he is back to form, Alcaraz responded, “I think so.” The U.S. Open is bringing that out in him. “I’m just trying to enjoy my time on the court,” Alcaraz said. “It doesn't matter that I was out four months and a half. Every time that I come here, I play my best.” Alcaraz will play Tuesday against American Ben Shelton, the No. 8 seed who swept Stefanos Tsitsipas on Sunday night in his strongest performance of the tournament. “We're happy to have him back on tour. He lights up the stadium every time he plays," Shelton said of Alcaraz. "I think it's going to be fireworks on Tuesday night.” Americans are making runs at the US Open Townsend and Paul were among the 10 Americans to reach the men’s and women’s round of 16. That is the most in the fourth round at any Grand Slam in nearly a quarter-century, going back to the 2002 U.S. Open, when there were 11. The five U.S. men — Paul, Shelton, Learner Tien, Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen — are the most at a major since eight in 1995 at Flushing Meadows. “American tennis has been on the up and up for many years now,” Townsend said. “There have been a really consistent chunk of players — Jess, Coco — (who) have been at the top and inside the top five for the last, I don’t know how many years. Ben, Frances, Tommy, Taylor: It’s just such a great group of men, as well.” At 20, Tien is the youngest American man in the U.S. Open fourth round since Andy Roddick in 2002. Tiafoe knocked off seventh-seeded Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (1), 6-4, 7-6 (6) to improve to 10-0 in his career at Louis Armstrong Stadium, which he called “the people's court." Michelsen beat Tomas Martin Etcheverry 7-6 (6), 6-4, 6-4. Michelsen and Tiafoe will meet in the quarterfinals Tuesday, guaranteeing an American man in the semifinals. No U.S. men's player has won a Grand Slam since Roddick in New York in '03. There could also be an all-American matchup in the women's quarterfinals. No. 3 Jessica Pegula got there by beating No. 16 Sorana Cirstea and awaited the winner of the match between 26th-seeded American Emma Navarro and Anna Kalinskaya.

articles.title: Expanded free college education law a 'major opportunity' for 4Ps families--Libanan
articles.summary: House Minority Leader and 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino “Nonoy” Libanan says the Expanded Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act opens up a "major opportunity" for poor Filipino families.…

blocks.text: House Minority Leader and 4Ps Party-list Rep. Marcelino “Nonoy” Libanan says the Expanded Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act opens up a "major opportunity" for poor Filipino families.

According to Libanan, high school graduates from the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps) now have a stronger pathway to a college education, thanks to this new law providing qualified students with financial assistance to pursue their chosen degree programs.

Moreover, the House leader said it assures high school graduates from 4Ps families of financial support, provided they meet the academic requirements for admission to a recognized higher education institution.

“This is a major opportunity for our 4Ps families. We want their children to have a fair chance to go to college, finish a degree and build a better future for themselves and their families,” Libanan said over the weekend.
President Marcos signed the Expanded Universal Access to Quality Tertiary Education Act, or Republic Act (RA) No. 12325, into law on Sept. 4.

Under the expanded free college education law, financial assistance may cover tuition and other school fees, as well as reasonable allowances for books, school supplies, transportation and miscellaneous personal expenses.
“When applicable, students may also receive assistance for room and board, as well as the documented rental or purchase of a personal computer,” Libanan said.

He added that qualified students in cities or municipalities without a state university or local government college may pursue their preferred programs in private higher education institutions and still receive financial assistance under the law.

“If the student’s chosen college program requires a professional license or certification, the financial aid will also help cover the one-time cost of obtaining the necessary credentials or qualifications, including applicable expenses for review classes and documentation,” noted the minority leader.
Libanan said the new law complements the government’s long-term investment in the education and human-capital development of poor Filipino families through 4Ps.

4Ps--the country's flagship poverty alleviation program--provides conditional cash grants to qualified poor households to help them meet their children’s health, nutrition and education needs. The program’s broader objective is to develop the capabilities of children and help families break the intergenerational cycle of poverty.

After 18 years of implementation, the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) said 4Ps has served 4.4 million Filipino families. Nearly 3 million households remain active beneficiaries, while almost 1.6 million Pantawid families have already reached self-sufficiency, according to the agency.

The DSWD also reported that 39,879 former 4Ps beneficiaries have passed professional board examinations, including 257 who emerged as topnotchers. In 2026 alone, 99 former 4Ps beneficiaries earned topnotcher honors in various professional licensure examinations.

The results are particularly encouraging in the field of education. The DSWD reported that 72 former 4Ps monitored children landed among the top ranks of the March 2026 Licensure Examination for Teachers (LET), including two who placed No. 1 in the elementary and secondary levels. Since 2019, a total of 154 former 4Ps monitored children have passed the LET.
For Libanan, these achievements demonstrate what can happen when children from poor families are given sustained support to remain in school, complete their education and pursue professional careers.
“These young Filipinos are proof that poverty should never be a barrier to excellence. Give our children the opportunity, and they can excel just like anyone else,” Libanan said.
He said expanding access to higher education is critical to ensuring that the gains made through 4Ps continue beyond the beneficiaries’ school years.

“Education remains one of the most powerful tools for breaking the cycle of poverty. By helping our 4Ps children reach college and earn professional qualifications, we are giving them a better chance to lift their families and communities to a higher standard of living,” Libanan said.

articles.title: Matcha Boom Drives Prices Up for Raw Material in Japan
articles.summary: Kagoshima, Sept. 4 (Jiji Press)--The global matcha boom is driving up prices in Japan for "tencha," the raw material for the finely ground green tea powder. The shipping price of tencha has more than…

blocks.text: Kagoshima, Sept. 4 (Jiji Press)--The global matcha boom is driving up prices in Japan for "tencha," the raw material for the finely ground green tea powder. The shipping price of tencha has more than doubled due to strong demand both at home and abroad. "People bought as much (matcha) as we had in stock," said Kenta Ikeda, CEO of Ikeda Seicha Co., a tea seller in Kagoshima Prefecture, southwestern Japan. He said that 30-gram canned matcha had been quickly sold out on sales websites last autumn when demand started surging. Moves by certain customers to buy up all cans have dissipated, but inquiries from home and abroad remain strong. The global boom began with the launch of Starbucks matcha latte in 2006, according to the Tea Industry Chamber of Kagoshima. The drink's healthy image gained attention, particularly in the United States, and its popularity soared last year as influencers showcased matcha on social media. The average shipping price of tencha rose for the fifth consecutive year in 2025, more than doubling from the previous year to 8,562 yen per kilogram, according to the Japanese Association of Tea Production. To capitalize on the boom, tea farmers are shifting from "sencha," the most popular Japanese tea, to tencha. As a result, production of sencha has sharply declined, making it expensive and less affordable. Toru Mitsumura, a senior official of the Tea Industry Chamber of Kagoshima, said that rising sencha prices have driven customers away, leading to "Japanese tea being replaced on supermarket shelves by barley tea and other beverages." He said that a possible loss of sencha enthusiasts could leave tea farmers in a difficult position once the matcha boom subsides.

articles.summary: Shirahama, Wakayama Pref., Sept. 4 (Jiji Press)--Two robotic penguins that move realistically are gaining popularity at the Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture,…

blocks.text: Shirahama, Wakayama Pref., Sept. 4 (Jiji Press)--Two robotic penguins that move realistically are gaining popularity at the Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture, western Japan.

blocks.caption: Ikuma Okada, who created the robotic penguins, is photographed with two of the robots at Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture, on July 30.

blocks.text: Ikuma Okada, who created the robotic penguins, is photographed with two of the robots at Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture, on July 30.

The robots--one modeled after a rockhopper penguin and the other after a gentoo penguin--are exhibited among real penguins at the theme park, the world's only facility to house 10 species of penguins.

Visitors looked amazed to see one of the robots deftly move its flippers to change direction and dive deeper into the water as it swam next to real Humboldt penguins. "I thought it was real," one visitor said.

blocks.caption: A robotic penguin swims in a pool at Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture, on July 30.

blocks.text: A robotic penguin swims in a pool at Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture, on July 30.
The robots were created by Ikuma Okada, a 34-year-old leader of a group within the Adventure World operator.

Established in 2019, the group began developing robotic animals to let people who cannot visit the park feel closer to animals. It has made robots of many types of animals, including dolphins and tuna.

"We take meticulous care to make (robots) as realistic as possible," Okada said. "If you look closely and notice that what you're looking at are robots, it can provide an opportunity to take a fresh look at real animals."
A robotic penguin (bottom left) swims next to real Humboldt penguins at Adventure World theme park in the town of Shirahama, Wakayama Prefecture, on July 30.
The robotic penguins are covered in a material used in wetsuits. Toothpicks were used to form feather-like patterns on the material. The robots are remotely controlled by staff members.
Okada said he plans to improve the robots, including by making them more waterproof and using highly wear-resistant parts, so that they can move automatically for longer periods.

It is held every September 7 to honor the 1923 founding of the International Criminal Police Organization (Interpol) and strengthen cross-border security ties.
Brig. Gen. Nestor Babagay, PRO-10 director, said local forces must work hand in hand with international agencies to keep modern criminals from finding safe havens in the provinces.
